grammarPages.titleEnglish: Introduce Someone with 叫, 姓, and 是
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Introduce someone by name, surname, or identity.
grammarPages.explanation: 叫, 姓 and 是 are used as verbs and equate two nouns in a sentence. 姓 comes only before a family name. 叫 comes before a given name or a full name. 是 says what someone is. Put 不 before them to say no.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 叫, 姓 and 是 are used as verbs and equate two nouns in a sentence. 姓 is only used for a family name. But 叫 can be used for either a given name or a full name.

items.answer: 姓 takes only a family name; use 叫 before a given name or full name.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe Someone with 很 or 不
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that someone is or is not busy, tired, or pretty.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 很 or 不 before adjectives like 漂亮, 可愛, 忙 and 累. These words already carry the meaning of "is", so no 是 is needed. 很 can mean "very"; 不 means "not".
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Adverbs 很 and 不 can be placed before a Vs. In this pattern, a Vs can be regarded as an adjective, but there is no need to add the verb “to be” because it is already embedded in the Intransitive State Verb.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask a Yes/No Question with 嗎
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Turn a statement into a yes-or-no question with one ending word.
grammarPages.explanation: Add 嗎 at the very end of the statement, without any change in order. Nothing inside the sentence moves. The listener answers yes or no.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: A question can be formed by adding 嗎 at the end of the statement without any change in order. It is close to a yes/no question in English.

patternRows.english: Is he Taiwanese?
Is she pretty?

text.simplified: A：他是日本人吗？ B：他不是日本人，他是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì Rìběn rén ma? B: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: Is he Japanese? B: He is not Japanese; he is Taiwanese.

text.english: Is he busy?

items.question: Where does 嗎 go?
items.answer: At the very end. The whole statement stays first, exactly in its order.

items.question: Do I keep 嗎 when I answer?
items.answer: No. 嗎 only asks a question; the answer is the plain statement.

right.pinyin: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
right.english: He is not Japanese; he is Taiwanese.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 呢 to Say “And You?”
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask the same question back with 呢, without repeating the whole sentence.
grammarPages.explanation: When a question is already in the air, say the new person or thing, add 呢, and stop. 呢 repeats that question for the new person without saying the sentence again.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 呢 is used at the end of the sentence in an abbreviated way to ask a question from the previous clause.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Count Things with Measure Words
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask for and say how many people, books, flowers, or gifts there are.
grammarPages.explanation: Chinese needs a measure word between a number and noun: 個 for general nouns, 本 for books, and 朵 for flowers. Before a measure word, say 兩 for “two,” not 二. 幾 (how many) is always used together with a measure word and is usually used when the amount is less than ten.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: When a noun is modified by a number, a measure word is necessary in order to specify a certain quantity. The number 二 becomes 兩 when there is a measure word used. 幾 (how many) is always used together with a measure word and is usually used when the amount is less than ten.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 這／那／哪 + 數字 + 量詞 + 名詞
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Point to This, That, or Which Thing
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Point to things that are near or far, or ask which one someone means.
grammarPages.explanation: Start with 這, 那, or 哪, then add the number, measure word, and noun. With one item, 一 is often omitted; with two, use 兩. 這, 那, and 哪 mean “this,” “that,” and “which.” Use 這 when the noun is close and 那 when it is far.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
These three words mean “this” “that” and “which”. It depends on the proximity of the nouns you are referring to. If it is close to you, use 這; if it is far, use 那.
When the number is one, we usually omit it. When the number is two, then change it to “兩”.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe a Noun or Replace It with 的
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe the thing you want and avoid repeating an obvious noun.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 的 to link a describing word to a noun. With short one-syllable words, you can usually skip 的. If the topic is already clear, drop the noun and keep just 的.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
When a Vs modifies a noun, 的 can be used between them.
(1) 的 is used between a Vs and a noun.
(2) 的 can be omitted.
We often omit 的 when it is used with one-syllable Vs.
(3) Nouns can be omitted.
Nouns, mentioned previously, can be omitted for subsequent usage to avoid repetition; however, the 的 cannot be omitted.

practice.title: Complete the following sentences with 也.

repairs.note: 都 sums up a group that comes before it; to add one more thing, use 也.
和 joins two nouns (牛肉麵和蛋糕), not two 要吃 parts: use 也.

items.fallbackRepair: 也 goes before the verb part: 也要吃蛋糕.

result.traditional: 我要吃牛肉麵，也要吃蛋糕。
result.simplified: 我要吃牛肉面，也要吃蛋糕。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yào chī niúròu miàn, yě yào chī dàngāo.
result.english: I want beef noodles, and I also want cake.

repairs.note: 好喝 is for drinks; cake is 好吃.
A asks what is good, and 也 means "the same as the noodles": 也很好吃, no 不.

items.fallbackRepair: The new subject comes first, then 也, then the description: 蛋糕也很好吃.

result.traditional: 牛肉麵很好吃，蛋糕也很好吃。
result.simplified: 牛肉面很好吃，蛋糕也很好吃。
result.pinyin: Niúròu miàn hěn hǎochī, dàngāo yě hěn hǎochī.
result.english: The beef noodles are delicious, and the cake is delicious too.

repairs.note: 賣 is "sell"; A asks who likes buying: 買.
都 needs a group before it (我們都喜歡); to add one more person, use 也.

items.fallbackRepair: The second person comes first, then 也 before the verb: 他也喜歡買.

result.traditional: 我喜歡買便宜的東西，他也喜歡買。
result.simplified: 我喜欢买便宜的东西，他也喜欢买。
result.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān mǎi piányi de dōngxi, tā yě xǐhuān mǎi.
result.english: I like buying cheap things, and he likes buying them too.

repairs.note: 都 sums up a group before it; to add one more "no", use 也: 也不喝.
和 joins nouns (咖啡和茶), not two 不喝 parts: use 也.
Tea is drunk: 喝, not 吃.

items.fallbackRepair: 也 comes before 不: 也不喝茶 ("don't drink tea either").

result.traditional: 我不喝咖啡，也不喝茶。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bù hē kāfēi, yě bù hē chá.
result.english: I don't drink coffee, and I don't drink tea either.

summary: Put 也 before the verb or adjective to say the same is true again.
It can be the same subject doing one more thing, or a different subject.
For a new subject, name it first, then 也, then repeat the verb: 他也買書.

repairs.note: Being cheap is no reason to say no; B won't buy it because it costs too much: 太貴了.
Looking good is no reason to say no; B's reason is the price: 太貴了.
很 only describes; 太…了 says it is more than B wants: 太貴了.

items.fallbackRepair: 太 goes before the describing word and 了 after it: 太貴了.

summary: Put 太 before a describing word and 了 after it to react strongly, like 太熱了.
It can mean too, or an excited so or really, depending on the situation.
As a full reaction, close it with 了. 太熱 alone is not enough.

subsections.title: Numerical System in Chinese
subsections.explanation: The blocks run 十 (10), 百 (100), 千 (1,000) and 萬 (10,000). Read the biggest part first, then what is left. When a middle place is empty, say 零 once; zeroes at the end are not read. In prices and amounts the last block word is often dropped (八百五 for 八百五十).

repairs.note: 八百 is 800; 800,000 is eighty 萬: 八十萬.
五十 is 50, but the 5 sits in the hundreds place: 五百.

result.traditional: 八十萬零五百。
result.simplified: 八十万零五百。
result.pinyin: Bāshí wàn líng wǔbǎi.

repairs.note: A phone number reads digits, and the digit 2 is 二; 兩 counts things (兩杯茶).
A phone number reads digits, and the digit 2 is 二; 兩 counts things (兩杯茶).
Read every digit on its own, 0 as 零: 零九三零, not 三十.

result.traditional: 零九三零二五二二四二。

repairs.note: Before 千, the number 2 is said 兩: 兩千.
本 counts books; people such as 老師 take 個.
零 fills a missing place; 2,200 has none between 千 and 百.

result.pinyin: Liǎngqiān liǎngbǎi ge lǎoshī.
result.english: 2,200 teachers.

repairs.note: Big numbers count in 萬 (four zeros), not 千: split off 0000 and read 940 萬.
九千…萬 would be 94,000,000; 9,400,000 is 940 萬: 九百四十萬.

summary: Build numbers with 十, 百, 千 and 萬. Read the biggest part first, then the rest.
If a middle place is empty, say 零 once, as in 一百零五. Zeroes at the end are not read.
In prices and amounts, the last block word is often dropped, so 一百五 is the short way to say 150.

多 can be used to express the number is in excess of a certain amount.
(1) Nu + 多 + M + N
(2) Nu + M + 多 + N

summary: After a round number, 多 means somewhere above it: 一百多 means 101 to 199.

summary: Put 得 right after a verb, then say how well the action is done.
With an object, repeat the verb, like 跑步跑得很快, or put the object first. The verb stays next to 得.
得 is not 的. 得 links an action to how it is done, and 的 shows belonging.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say “A Little” with 有一點兒
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a small, often inconvenient degree: a little tired, cold, or small.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 有一點兒 (or 有點兒) before a describing word to say it is slightly so — usually for a small problem.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 有（一）點（兒）is used as an adverb to express slightly/a little, modifying the Vs that follows it.

discoveryLab.title: Turn up only one notch

contrast.title: A little vs. a little amount

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask and Give Permission with 可以
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Offer a possible solution or ask whether an action is permitted.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 可以 to ask for permission or suggest a solution. Ask with 可以…嗎 or 可不可以. Answer with 可以 to allow it, or 不可以 to say no.

teachingGlossary.meaning: may or may not; can or cannot
shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 可以 + Verb; Subject + 可以 + Verb 嗎？

discoveryLab.title: Read the green-light card

choices.label: Suggestion

contrast.title: Learned ability or permission
contrast.description: Both can translate as “can,” but they answer different questions.

items.label: Permission
items.note: 可以 asks whether the action is allowed.

items.question: May I go to the restroom? Is it 我去可以洗手間嗎?
items.answer: Put 可以 before the verb 去.

right.traditional: 老師，我現在可以去洗手間嗎？
right.simplified: 老师，我现在可以去洗手间吗？
right.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ xiànzài kěyǐ qù xǐshǒujiān ma?
right.english: Teacher, may I go to the restroom now?

items.question: To ask Mom if I may have ice cream, can I say 我想吃冰淇淋嗎?
items.answer: No — 想 means want. To ask permission, use 可以: 我可以吃冰淇淋嗎？

right.english: May I eat ice cream?

items.question: Do I add 嗎 after 可不可以, like 可以不可以去嗎?
items.answer: No — 可不可以 is already a question. Adding 嗎 doubles the question ending.

right.traditional: 我們可不可以在捷運上吃東西？
right.simplified: 我们可不可以在捷运上吃东西？
right.pinyin: Wǒmen kě bù kěyǐ zài jiéyùn shàng chī dōngxi?
right.english: May we eat on the metro?

text.english: A: I do not know what gift to give Mom. B: You can give her a new red item of clothing.

text.simplified: A：你想要点什么？ B：这里的珍珠奶茶很好喝，我们可以点（珍珠奶茶）。

text.simplified: A：妈妈，我可以吃冰淇淋吗？ B：太冷了，不可以。
text.pinyin: A: Māma, wǒ kěyǐ chī bīngqílín ma? B: Tài lěng le, bù kěyǐ.

text.traditional: A：老師，我現在可以去洗手間嗎？ B：可以。

text.english: A: Teacher, may I go to the restroom now? B: Yes.

text.traditional: A：我們可不可以在捷運上吃東西？ B：不可以，也不可以喝飲料。
text.simplified: A：我们可不可以在捷运上吃东西？ B：不可以，也不可以喝饮料。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen kě bù kěyǐ zài jiéyùn shàng chī dōngxi? B: Bù kěyǐ, yě bù kěyǐ hē yǐnliào.

repairs.note: 會 is a skill you learned; to suggest something, use 可以.

repairs.note: 會 is a skill you learned; to suggest something, use 可以.

items.fallbackRepair: 可以 comes before the action: 可以去洗手間.

scene.alt: Two people at a library desk beside bookshelves and a library sign.

repairs.note: Asking permission takes 可以; 會 is a learned skill.
Answer with the question’s verb: 可以, not 是.
Look at the picture: it’s a library, so reading is fine. Ask and answer with 可以.

items.fallbackRepair: Ask with 可以, and answer with 可以.

result.traditional: 我可以在這裡看書嗎？可以。
result.simplified: 我可以在这里看书吗？可以。
result.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ kàn shū ma? Kěyǐ.

segments.traditional: 游泳，可是媽媽說我今天
segments.simplified: 游泳，可是妈妈说我今天

repairs.note: This sentence needs 會 (a skill) and 不可以 (not allowed); 沒 goes with neither.
是 doesn’t go before a verb: use 會 (a skill) or 可以 (allowed).

items.fallbackRepair: 會 = know how (a skill): 會游泳. 可以 = allowed: 不可以去.

result.traditional: 我會游泳，可是媽媽說我今天不可以去。

result.english: I can swim, but Mom says I can't go today.

summary: Use 可以 to ask for permission or to suggest a way to solve a problem.
Ask with 可以 and 嗎, or with 可不可以. Answer with 可以 or 不可以.
Put 可以 before the verb, and don't add 嗎 after 可不可以.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 從 and 到: From and To
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where someone comes from and where they go.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 means from. 到 means to. Put the place right after it, then end with 來 (come) or 去 (go).
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This sentence pattern is used to convey someone departing from somewhere or going to somewhere.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 從 / 到 + place + 來 / 去

items.question: Which place follows 從?
items.answer: Put the starting place after 從 and the destination after 到.
items.wrongTraditional: 我到學校從我家去上課。

right.traditional: 我從我家到學校去上課。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng wǒ jiā dào xuéxiào qù shàngkè.
right.english: I go to school from my home for class.
right.simplified: 我从我家到学校去上课。

items.question: He is coming to my home; 來 or 去?
items.answer: Use 來 because the trip ends at the speaker’s home.

scene.alt: A flight arrow points from the United States toward Taiwan.

repairs.note: He is coming to see me (看我), so he moves toward the speaker: 來, not 去.

items.fallbackRepair: Follow the arrow: 從 + where he starts, 到 + where he goes, then 來: 從美國到台灣來.

result.traditional: 他從美國到台灣來看我。
result.simplified: 他从美国到台湾来看我。
result.pinyin: Tā cóng Měiguó dào Táiwān lái kàn wǒ.
result.english: He is coming from the United States to Taiwan to see me.

scene.alt: A man leaves a house and walks along an arrow toward a school.

repairs.note: You are at home and he walks away from you, so the sentence ends in 去, not 來.

items.fallbackRepair: Follow the arrow: 從 + the house, 到 + the school, then 去: 從家到學校去.

result.traditional: 我在家，他從家到學校去。
result.simplified: 我在家，他从家到学校去。
result.pinyin: Wǒ zài jiā, tā cóng jiā dào xuéxiào qù.
result.english: I am at home; he goes from home to school.

scene.alt: A man follows an arrow from the restaurant toward the library.

repairs.note: 在 only says where someone is; for a trip, 從 marks the start and 到 the place he goes.

items.fallbackRepair: Follow the arrow: 從餐廳 (start), 到圖書館 (goal), then 去 and why he goes.

result.traditional: 他從餐廳到圖書館去看書。
result.simplified: 他从餐厅到图书馆去看书。
result.pinyin: Tā cóng cāntīng dào túshūguǎn qù kàn shū.
result.english: He goes from the restaurant to the library to read.

summary: 從 means from and 到 means to. Put where you start after 從 and where you go after 到.
Use both in one sentence, start first and then the end: 從我家到學校.
After the place, say 來 (come) or 去 (go).
Use 來 when the trip ends where the speaker is: 到我家來.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 怎麼: How You Get There
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask and say how someone travels.
grammarPages.explanation: Ask with 怎麼 (how). Answer with how you travel, like 坐公車, 騎腳踏車 or 走路, then 來 or 去.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern expresses how to get around with transportation or on foot.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + travel method + 來 / 去

patternRows.english: How do you get there?
I get there by bus.

items.question: Do I use 坐 with 走路?
items.answer: Use 走路 for walking, without 坐.
items.wrongTraditional: 我不要坐走路去，我要坐捷運去。

right.traditional: A：你要走路去嗎？ B：我不要走路去，我要坐捷運去。
right.simplified: A：你要走路去吗？ B：我不要走路去，我要坐捷运去。
right.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào zǒulù qù ma? B: Wǒ bú yào zǒulù qù, wǒ yào zuò jiéyùn qù.
right.english: A: Are you going to walk? B: I am not going to walk; I am going by MRT.

items.question: Does the travel method go before 去?
items.answer: Put 坐公車 before 去 when it answers how you travel.

right.english: I get there by bus.

items.question: Where does 怎麼 go?
items.answer: Put 怎麼 before 去 to ask how you get there.

right.english: How do you get there?

text.traditional: A：你們怎麼來？ B：我們騎腳踏車來。
text.simplified: A：你们怎么来？ B：我们骑脚踏车来。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen zěnme lái? B: Wǒmen qí jiǎotàchē lái.
text.english: A: How are you all coming? B: We are coming by bicycle.

text.traditional: A：你要走路去嗎？ B：我不要走路去，我要坐捷運去。
text.simplified: A：你要走路去吗？ B：我不要走路去，我要坐捷运去。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào zǒulù qù ma? B: Wǒ bú yào zǒulù qù, wǒ yào zuò jiéyùn qù.
text.english: A: Are you going to walk? B: I am not going to walk; I am going by MRT.

text.traditional: A：他坐公車到學校去嗎？ B：不，他坐計程車到學校去。
text.simplified: A：他坐公车到学校去吗？ B：不，他坐计程车到学校去。
text.pinyin: A: Tā zuò gōngchē dào xuéxiào qù ma? B: Bù, tā zuò jìchéngchē dào xuéxiào qù.
text.english: A: Is he taking the bus to school? B: No, he is taking a taxi to school.

repairs.note: You are both at school, away from his place, so getting there ends in 去, not 來.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, then how (怎麼), then 到 + place + 去: 你怎麼到他家去？

result.traditional: 我們在學校，你怎麼到他家去？
result.simplified: 我们在学校，你怎么到他家去？
result.pinyin: Wǒmen zài xuéxiào, nǐ zěnme dào tā jiā qù?
result.english: We are at school. How do you get to his place?

alternatives.traditional: 我們在學校，你到他家怎麼去？
alternatives.simplified: 我们在学校，你到他家怎么去？
alternatives.pinyin: Wǒmen zài xuéxiào, nǐ dào tā jiā zěnme qù?
alternatives.english: We are at school. How do you get to his place?

repairs.note: 騎 is for a bike you sit astride (騎腳踏車); a bus takes 坐: 坐公車.

items.fallbackRepair: When, then how (坐公車), then 到學校來: 他每天坐公車到學校來.

result.traditional: 他每天坐公車到學校來。
result.simplified: 他每天坐公车到学校来。
result.pinyin: Tā měi tiān zuò gōngchē dào xuéxiào lái.
result.english: He comes to school by bus every day.

repairs.note: The hotel is too far from you, so you would be going away from where you are: 去, not 來.

items.fallbackRepair: 不要 comes first, then how (走路), then 到 + place + 去: 我不要走路到那家飯店去.

result.traditional: 我不要走路到那家飯店去，太遠了。
result.simplified: 我不要走路到那家饭店去，太远了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bú yào zǒulù dào nà jiā fàndiàn qù, tài yuǎn le.
result.english: I don’t want to walk to that hotel; it’s too far.

summary: Ask how to get somewhere by putting 怎麼 before 去: 你怎麼去.
To answer, say how you travel, like 坐公車 or 走路, then 來 or 去.
走路 doesn't take 坐.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: 了: Something Changed
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something is new or has changed.
grammarPages.explanation: 了 at the end of a sentence means something is new: it was not true before, but it is now.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: When there is a new situation, 了 can be placed at the end of the sentence to express the change.

items.question: Where does 了 go with 餓?
items.answer: Put 了 after 餓 to show the new state.

right.english: I am hungry now.

items.question: Where does 了 go in 可以上車了?
items.answer: Put 了 after the whole action 可以上車.

right.english: We can get on the bus now.

items.question: Can 不可以 follow the action here?
items.answer: Put 不可以 before 玩手機 to say it is no longer allowed.
items.wrongTraditional: 上課了，老師來了，我們玩手機不可以了。

right.traditional: 上課了，老師來了，我們不可以玩手機了。
right.simplified: 上课了，老师来了，我们不可以玩手机了。
right.pinyin: Shàngkè le, lǎoshī lái le, wǒmen bù kěyǐ wán shǒujī le.
right.english: Class has started and the teacher is here; we cannot play on our phones anymore.

discoveryLab.title: Ring the change bell
discoveryLab.description: See the moment when a state becomes true for the first time.

choices.label: Example 1
choices.pinyin: Wǒ è le, xiǎng chī yìdiǎn dōngxi.
choices.english: I am hungry; I want to eat something.
choices.note: Read 了 at the end of the new situation.

choices.label: Example 2
choices.traditional: 孩子都累了，我們一起休息吧！
choices.simplified: 孩子都累了，我们一起休息吧！
choices.pinyin: Háizi dōu lèi le, wǒmen yìqǐ xiūxí ba!
choices.english: The children are all tired; let us take a rest together!
choices.note: Read 了 at the end of the new situation.

choices.label: Example 3
choices.traditional: 啊！現在十點了！我的錶慢了。
choices.simplified: 啊！现在十点了！我的表慢了。
choices.pinyin: Ā! Xiànzài shí diǎn le! Wǒ de biǎo màn le.
choices.english: Oh! It is ten o’clock now! My watch is slow.
choices.note: Read 了 at the end of the new situation.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Use 了 when "now it is different" matters.

text.traditional: 我餓了，想吃一點東西。
text.simplified: 我饿了，想吃一点东西。
text.pinyin: Wǒ è le, xiǎng chī yìdiǎn dōngxi.
text.english: I am hungry; I want to eat something.

text.traditional: 孩子都累了，我們一起休息吧！
text.simplified: 孩子都累了，我们一起休息吧！
text.pinyin: Háizi dōu lèi le, wǒmen yìqǐ xiūxí ba!
text.english: The children are all tired; let us take a rest together!

text.traditional: 啊！現在十點了！我的錶慢了。
text.simplified: 啊！现在十点了！我的表慢了。
text.pinyin: Ā! Xiànzài shí diǎn le! Wǒ de biǎo màn le.
text.english: Oh! It is ten o’clock now! My watch is slow.

text.traditional: 你十五歲了，應該學做飯了。
text.simplified: 你十五岁了，应该学做饭了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ shíwǔ suì le, yīnggāi xué zuòfàn le.
text.english: You are fifteen now; you should learn to cook.

text.traditional: 上課了，老師來了，我們不可以玩手機了。
text.simplified: 上课了，老师来了，我们不可以玩手机了。
text.pinyin: Shàngkè le, lǎoshī lái le, wǒmen bù kěyǐ wán shǒujī le.
text.english: Class has started and the teacher is here; we cannot play on our phones anymore.

text.traditional: A：請你明天早上九點來。 B：好，我知道了，謝謝。
text.simplified: A：请你明天早上九点来。 B：好，我知道了，谢谢。

subsections.title: Adjective + 了
subsections.explanation: A new feeling or state: 餓了 means hungry now.

patternRows.english: I am hungry now.

subsections.title: Verb + 了
subsections.explanation: Something starts to happen, or can happen now: 來了, 可以上車了.

patternRows.english: The bus is coming.
We can get on the bus now.

exerciseCues.label: Picture 1
exerciseCues.detail: Yesterday: 25°C → Today: 30°C.

exerciseCues.label: Teacher and students
exerciseCues.detail: You understand the correction now.

scene.alt: Yesterday was 25°C; today is 30°C.

repairs.note: Yesterday 25°C, today 30°C: it got hotter, so 熱, not 冷.
熱 is a state verb; it never takes 是.
This is a statement about the picture, not a question; a change ends in 了.

items.fallbackRepair: The quality first, then 了 at the very end: 熱了.

result.traditional: 今天天氣熱了。
result.simplified: 今天天气热了。
result.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì rè le.
result.english: It has gotten hot today.

scene.alt: A bowl costs $80 in 2016 and $120 now.

repairs.note: The price went from $80 to $120, so things got more expensive: 貴, not 便宜.
貴 needs no 的 here; mark the change with 了 at the end.
This is a statement about the picture, not a question; a change ends in 了.

items.fallbackRepair: The quality first, then 了 at the very end: 貴了.

result.traditional: 現在東西都貴了。
result.simplified: 现在东西都贵了。
result.pinyin: Xiànzài dōngxi dōu guì le.
result.english: Everything has gotten expensive now.

segments.traditional: 不可以說「吃飯得很快」，應該說「吃飯吃得很快」，你們
segments.simplified: 不可以说「吃饭得很快」，应该说「吃饭吃得很快」，你们

repairs.note: The student thanks the teacher, so they do understand now: no 不.
The teacher’s question already ends in 嗎, and the student’s reply needs none.

items.fallbackRepair: 懂 comes before 了: 懂了.

result.traditional: 不可以說「吃飯得很快」，應該說「吃飯吃得很快」，你們懂了嗎？懂了！謝謝老師。
result.simplified: 不可以说「吃饭得很快」，应该说「吃饭吃得很快」，你们懂了吗？懂了！谢谢老师。
result.pinyin: Bù kěyǐ shuō “chīfàn de hěn kuài”, yīnggāi shuō “chīfàn chī de hěn kuài”, nǐmen dǒng le ma? Dǒng le! Xièxie lǎoshī.
result.english: You can’t say “chīfàn de hěn kuài”; you should say “chīfàn chī de hěn kuài”. Do you understand now? I get it now! Thank you, teacher.

repairs.note: B just said no to coffee, so B isn’t going to drink; B is going to sleep.
睡覺 is an action; it takes no 是.
B is answering, not asking; the new plan ends in 了.

items.fallbackRepair: 要 + the action, then 了 at the very end: 我要睡覺了.

result.traditional: 不要，謝謝。我要睡覺了。
result.simplified: 不要，谢谢。我要睡觉了。
result.pinyin: Bú yào, xièxie. Wǒ yào shuìjiào le.
result.english: No, thanks. I’m going to bed now.

summary: Put 了 at the end of a sentence to say something is new: it wasn't true before, but it is now.
After an adjective, it shows a new state, like 餓了.
After a verb, it shows something starts or can happen now, like 可以上車了.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 學校的下課休息時間 · Break time at school

text.traditional: 元真，我們明天幾點去找妳的韓國朋友？
text.simplified: 元真，我们明天几点去找你的韩国朋友？
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn, wǒmen míngtiān jǐ diǎn qù zhǎo nǐ de Hánguó péngyǒu?
text.english: Yuanzhen, what time are we going to meet up with your Korean friends tomorrow?

text.traditional: 我們下午四點要到天美飯店，她在那裡等我們。
text.simplified: 我们下午四点要到天美饭店，她在那里等我们。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàwǔ sì diǎn yào dào Tiānměi Fàndiàn, tā zài nàlǐ děng wǒmen.
text.english: We have to arrive at Tianmei Hotel at 4 in the afternoon. She will wait for us there.

text.traditional: 我們要怎麼去？坐捷運還是坐公車？

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say the Activity First
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Name an activity first, then comment on it.
grammarPages.explanation: In Chinese, you can say the activity first, then say what you think about it. Think: activity → your comment.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Verb-objects can be placed to the beginning of a sentence to serve as a topic.

patternRows.english: Taking the MRT is very convenient.

columns.meaning: we all like it very much

patternRows.english: Playing soccer, we all like (it) very much.

items.question: Can I split 坐捷運 with the comment?
items.answer: Keep the activity 坐捷運 together before 很方便.

right.english: Taking the MRT is very convenient.

items.question: Does 都 go after 喜歡?
items.answer: Put 都 before 喜歡 in the comment 我都喜歡.
items.wrongTraditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我喜歡都。

right.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
right.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
right.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuan.
right.english: Running, swimming, and playing tennis — I like them all.

discoveryLab.title: Put the activity on stage
discoveryLab.description: The first chunk is what we are talking about; the rest is the comment.

choices.label: Example 1

choices.label: Example 2

choices.label: Example 3
choices.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。

choices.english: Running, swimming, and playing tennis — I like them all.
choices.note: Read the activity before its comment.

Keep the activity together before the comment.
If you list several activities, put 都 before the verb in the comment: 我都喜歡.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Pair Two True Qualities
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe two qualities or abilities that are true at the same time.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 又 before each of two qualities or actions describing the same subject; do not put nouns directly after 又.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This double 又 structure is like “both... and...”. It is used to describe two qualities to the subject. However, 又 can not be followed by nouns.
grammarPages.pattern: Person or thing + 又 + quality 1 + 又 + quality 2

patternRows.english: Taipei MRT is both fast and convenient.
He can both sing and paint.

items.question: Does each quality need 又?
items.answer: Put 又 before 快 and again before 方便.

right.traditional: 台北的捷運又快又方便。
right.pinyin: Táiběi de jiéyùn yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn.
right.english: Taipei MRT is both fast and convenient.
right.simplified: 台北的捷运又快又方便。

items.question: Can 又 stand before 他?
items.answer: Put 又 before each ability, after the subject 他.

right.pinyin: Tā yòu huì chànggē yòu huì huàhuà.
right.english: He can both sing and paint.

discoveryLab.title: Balance the two sides
discoveryLab.description: Each 又 opens one matching description. Both sides describe the same person or thing.

choices.label: Example 1
choices.traditional: 我同學的妹妹又可愛又漂亮。
choices.simplified: 我同学的妹妹又可爱又漂亮。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ tóngxué de mèimei yòu kě’ài yòu piàoliang.
choices.english: My classmate’s younger sister is both cute and pretty.
choices.note: Find 又 before each quality or action.

choices.label: Example 2
choices.traditional: 我現在又餓又渴，想喝一點兒茶、吃一點兒飯。
choices.simplified: 我现在又饿又渴，想喝一点儿茶、吃一点儿饭。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòu è yòu kě, xiǎng hē yìdiǎnr chá, chī yìdiǎnr fàn.
choices.english: I am both hungry and thirsty right now; I want to drink some tea and eat a little rice.
choices.note: Find 又 before each quality or action.

choices.label: Example 3
choices.traditional: 他又想去日本，又想去韓國，不知道應該先去哪國。
choices.simplified: 他又想去日本，又想去韩国，不知道应该先去哪国。
choices.pinyin: Tā yòu xiǎng qù Rìběn, yòu xiǎng qù Hánguó, bù zhīdào yīnggāi xiān qù nǎ guó.
choices.english: He wants to go to Japan and also wants to go to Korea; he does not know which country to visit first.
choices.note: Find 又 before each quality or action.

discoveryLab.takeaway: One person or thing, two matching 又 blocks.

text.traditional: 我同學的妹妹又可愛又漂亮。
text.simplified: 我同学的妹妹又可爱又漂亮。
text.pinyin: Wǒ tóngxué de mèimei yòu kě’ài yòu piàoliang.

text.english: I am both hungry and thirsty right now; I want to drink some tea and eat a little rice.

practice.title: Complete the following sentences with 又……又…….

repairs.note: B doesn’t like it, so both qualities are bad: 不舒服, not 舒服.
In 又……又……, each quality takes its own 又, not 很.

items.fallbackRepair: Put 又 before each quality: 又熱又不舒服.

segments.traditional: 你覺得這家餐廳的牛肉麵怎麼樣？
segments.simplified: 你觉得这家餐厅的牛肉面怎么样？

repairs.note: B likes it a lot, so both qualities are good ones: 好吃 and 便宜, not 貴.
和 joins nouns; two qualities take 又 before each one.

items.fallbackRepair: Put 又 before each quality: 又好吃又便宜.

result.traditional: 又好吃又便宜，我很喜歡。

result.pinyin: Yòu hǎochī yòu piányi, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
result.english: It’s both delicious and cheap; I like it a lot.

alternatives.traditional: 又便宜又好吃，我很喜歡。
alternatives.simplified: 又便宜又好吃，我很喜欢。
alternatives.pinyin: Yòu piányi yòu hǎochī, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
alternatives.english: It’s both cheap and delicious; I like it a lot.

segments.traditional: 曬太陽，每個週末都去海邊。
segments.simplified: 晒太阳，每个周末都去海边。

repairs.note: He goes to the beach every weekend, so he likes both: 喜歡, not 不喜歡.

items.fallbackRepair: 又 comes before each verb: 又喜歡游泳又喜歡曬太陽.

result.traditional: 他又喜歡游泳又喜歡曬太陽，每個週末都去海邊。
result.simplified: 他又喜欢游泳又喜欢晒太阳，每个周末都去海边。
result.pinyin: Tā yòu xǐhuan yóuyǒng yòu xǐhuan shài tàiyáng, měi ge zhōumò dōu qù hǎibiān.
result.english: He likes both swimming and sunbathing; he goes to the beach every weekend.

repairs.note: 又 is never followed by a noun; join two things with 和.
還是 (“or”) is for questions; in a statement, join two things with 和.
也 goes before a verb, not between two things; join them with 和.

items.fallbackRepair: Thing, 和, thing: 水果和茶.

result.traditional: 我要買水果和茶。
result.simplified: 我要买水果和茶。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi shuǐguǒ hé chá.
result.english: I’m going to buy fruit and tea.

alternatives.traditional: 我要買茶和水果。
alternatives.simplified: 我要买茶和水果。
alternatives.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi chá hé shuǐguǒ.
alternatives.english: I’m going to buy tea and fruit.

summary: Put 又 before each of two qualities or actions of the same subject, like 又快又方便.
Say the subject first, then 又 before each quality or action.
Don't put a noun directly after 又.

text.traditional: 友美，妳看，天美飯店在大學路。我現在知道怎麼走了。
text.simplified: 友美，你看，天美饭店在大学路。我现在知道怎么走了。

text.traditional: （看地圖）啊！天美飯店在這裡！我知道這個地方，附近有郵局跟超級市場。

text.traditional: 我想走路去一定沒問題。
text.simplified: 我想走路去一定没问题。

text.traditional: 妳想怎麼去？

grammarPages.titleEnglish: 好 / 難 + Verb
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what is pleasant or easy to do.
grammarPages.explanation: 好 or 難 before a perception verb says something is pleasant or unpleasant. Before an action verb, it says something is easy or hard to do.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
(1) Something is good or bad to do (perception verbs).
(2) Something is easy or difficult to do (action verbs).

text.traditional: 這家餐廳的牛肉麵很好吃，我常吃。
text.simplified: 这家餐厅的牛肉面很好吃，我常吃。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de niúròu miàn hěn hǎochī, wǒ cháng chī.
text.english: The beef noodles is delicious from this restaurant; I have (it) often.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

text.traditional: 這杯茶有點兒難喝，我不要喝。
text.simplified: 这杯茶有点儿难喝，我不要喝。
text.pinyin: Zhè bēi chá yǒu diǎnr nánhē, wǒ bú yào hē.
text.english: This cup of tea tastes a bit bad; I don’t want to drink it.

text.traditional: 這件衣服的顏色很好看，我很喜歡。
text.simplified: 这件衣服的颜色很好看，我很喜欢。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de yánsè hěn hǎokàn, wǒ hěn xǐhuān.
text.english: The color of this piece of clothing is good; I like it very much.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

text.traditional: 你唱歌唱得很好聽，現在唱一首，好嗎？
text.simplified: 你唱歌唱得很好听，现在唱一首，好吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ chàng gē chàng de hěn hǎotīng, xiànzài chàng yì shǒu, hǎo ma?
text.english: You sing very well. Can you do it now?

words.meaning: links an action to how well it is done

text.traditional: 這首中文歌很好唱，我朋友都會唱。
text.simplified: 这首中文歌很好唱，我朋友都会唱。
text.pinyin: Zhè shǒu Zhōngwén gē hěn hǎochàng, wǒ péngyǒu dōu huì chàng.
text.english: This Chinese song is easy to sing; all of my friends can sing it.

text.traditional: 弟弟不喜歡說英文，他覺得英文很難學。
text.simplified: 弟弟不喜欢说英文，他觉得英文很难学。
text.pinyin: Dìdi bù xǐhuān shuō Yīngwén, tā juéde Yīngwén hěn nánxué.
text.english: My younger brother doesn’t like to speak English; he thinks it is difficult to learn.

text.traditional: 這裡附近只有一家百貨公司，很好找。
text.simplified: 这里附近只有一家百货公司，很好找。

practice.title: Use 好 or 難 with perception verbs or action verbs to complete the following sentences.

repairs.note: You like the film, so it is good to watch: 好, not 難.
A film is watched, not listened to: 看. 好聽 is for songs and voices.

items.fallbackRepair: 好 or 難 comes first, then the verb: 好看.

result.traditional: 這部電影很好看，我很喜歡。
result.simplified: 这部电影很好看，我很喜欢。
result.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn, wǒ hěn xǐhuān.
result.english: This movie is really good; I like it a lot.

repairs.note: You like the new bike, so it is easy to ride: 好騎.
好穿 is for clothes and shoes; a bike is ridden: 騎.
走 is walking; a bike is ridden: 騎.

items.fallbackRepair: 好 comes first, then the verb: 好騎.

result.traditional: 新的腳踏車很好騎，我很喜歡。
result.simplified: 新的脚踏车很好骑，我很喜欢。
result.pinyin: Xīn de jiǎotàchē hěn hǎoqí, wǒ hěn xǐhuān.
result.english: The new bike is really easy to ride; I like it a lot.

repairs.note: You want to learn it too, so what you heard is good news: 好學.
好唱 is for songs; swimming is something you learn: 學.
好找 is for places; swimming is something you learn: 學.

items.fallbackRepair: 好 comes first, then the verb: 好學.

result.traditional: 聽說游泳很好學，我也想學。
result.simplified: 听说游泳很好学，我也想学。
result.pinyin: Tīngshuō yóuyǒng hěn hǎoxué, wǒ yě xiǎng xué.
result.english: I hear swimming is easy to learn; I want to learn too.

segments.traditional: 我覺得這張畫他畫得不好，有點兒
segments.simplified: 我觉得这张画他画得不好，有点儿

repairs.note: He drew it badly, and 有點兒 marks something unpleasant: 難看.
A picture is looked at, not listened to: 看.
難找 means hard to find; the problem is how it looks: 看.

items.fallbackRepair: 難 comes first, then the verb: 難看.

result.traditional: 我覺得這張畫他畫得不好，有點兒難看。
result.simplified: 我觉得这张画他画得不好，有点儿难看。
result.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè zhāng huà tā huà de bù hǎo, yǒu diǎnr nánkàn.
result.english: I think he didn't draw this picture well; it's a bit ugly.

repairs.note: Everyone wants to buy a cup, so it tastes good: 好喝.
Milk tea is drunk, not eaten: 好喝.

items.fallbackRepair: 好 comes first, then the verb: 好喝.

result.traditional: 珍珠奶茶很好喝，大家都想買一杯。
result.simplified: 珍珠奶茶很好喝，大家都想买一杯。
result.pinyin: Zhēnzhū nǎichá hěn hǎohē, dàjiā dōu xiǎng mǎi yì bēi.
result.english: Bubble milk tea is delicious; everyone wants to buy a cup.

repairs.note: 又…又… joins two of a kind: 遠 is a minus and you don't want to go, so 難.
難學 is for things you learn; a place can be hard to find: 找.
難聽 is for sounds; a place can be hard to find: 找.

items.fallbackRepair: 難 comes first, then the verb: 難找.

result.traditional: 那個地方又遠又難找，我不想跟你去。
result.simplified: 那个地方又远又难找，我不想跟你去。
result.pinyin: Nà ge dìfāng yòu yuǎn yòu nánzhǎo, wǒ bù xiǎng gēn nǐ qù.
result.english: That place is far and hard to find; I don't want to go with you.

summary: Put 好 or 難 before a verb for taste, looks or sound to say it is pleasant or unpleasant: 好吃.
Before an action verb, 好 or 難 says the action is easy or hard to do, like 難學.
Put them before the verb, not after it.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Cause and Effect
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give a reason and its result.
grammarPages.explanation: 因為 introduces the reason; 所以 introduces the result. The reason usually comes first.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, two clauses are connected in one cause-effect sentence. The clause with 因為 usually comes first to state the reason, followed by the other one with 所以 to state the result.
grammarPages.pattern: 因為 + reason, 所以 + result

patternRows.english: Because this is a very famous brand and its clothes are beautiful, many people like it.

text.traditional: A：你為什麼不想走路到學校去？ B：因為學校很遠，所以我不想走路到學校去。
text.simplified: A：你为什么不想走路到学校去？ B：因为学校很远，所以我不想走路到学校去。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ wèishénme bù xiǎng zǒu lù dào xuéxiào qù? B: Yīnwèi xuéxiào hěn yuǎn, suǒyǐ wǒ bù xiǎng zǒu lù dào xuéxiào qù.
text.english: A: Why don’t you want to walk to school? B: Because school is far away, I don’t want to walk there.

text.traditional: A：為什麼你的朋友不跟你來？ B：因為他很累，所以他要在家休息。
text.simplified: A：为什么你的朋友不跟你来？ B：因为他很累，所以他要在家休息。
text.pinyin: A: Wèishénme nǐ de péngyǒu bù gēn nǐ lái? B: Yīnwèi tā hěn lèi, suǒyǐ tā yào zài jiā xiūxí.
text.english: A: Why isn’t your friend coming with you? B: Because he is tired, he wants to rest at home.

items.question: Do 因為 and 所以 go together at the start?
items.answer: Put 因為 before the reason and 所以 before the result.

sentenceSpine.title: Read the pattern
sentenceSpine.description: 因為 introduces the reason; 所以 introduces the result. The reason usually comes first.
sentenceSpine.positiveEnglish: Because this is a very famous brand and its clothes are beautiful, many people like it.

subject.label: Reason
subject.traditional: 因為這個牌子很有名，衣服也很好看
subject.simplified: 因为这个牌子很有名，衣服也很好看
subject.pinyin: yīnwèi zhè ge páizi hěn yǒumíng, yīfu yě hěn hǎokàn
subject.english: because this is a famous brand and its clothes are beautiful

segments.traditional: 他為什麼常常穿綠色的衣服？
segments.simplified: 他为什么常常穿绿色的衣服？

repairs.note: He wears green often, so he must like it: 很喜歡, not 不.
Being afraid of green would not make him wear it: 喜歡.
Wearing it often is the result of liking it: 所以, not 可是.

items.fallbackRepair: The reason first, 因為他很喜歡綠色, then the result: 所以常常穿.

result.traditional: 因為他很喜歡綠色，所以常常穿。
result.simplified: 因为他很喜欢绿色，所以常常穿。
result.pinyin: Yīnwèi tā hěn xǐhuān lǜsè, suǒyǐ chángcháng chuān.
result.english: Because he really likes green, he wears it often.

segments.traditional: 因為我想游泳，也想曬太陽，所以想去海邊玩。
segments.simplified: 因为我想游泳，也想晒太阳，所以想去海边玩。

repairs.note: B answers with 因為, a reason, so A asked why: 為什麼, not 什麼 (what).
B answers with 因為, a reason, so A asked 為什麼; a 嗎 question gets 是 or 不.
A asks B about B's plan: 你.

items.fallbackRepair: A asks why: 你為什麼想去海邊玩？

result.traditional: 你為什麼想去海邊玩？
result.simplified: 你为什么想去海边玩？
result.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme xiǎng qù hǎibiān wán?
result.english: Why do you want to go to the beach?

alternatives.traditional: 為什麼你想去海邊玩？
alternatives.simplified: 为什么你想去海边玩？
alternatives.pinyin: Wèishénme nǐ xiǎng qù hǎibiān wán?
alternatives.english: Why do you want to go to the beach?

repairs.note: Going to Taiwan is the reason and learning Chinese the result: 因為…所以…, no contrast.
為什麼 asks the question; the answer gives the reason with 因為 and the result with 所以.

items.fallbackRepair: 因為 opens the reason, 所以 opens the result: 因為我想去台灣，所以我想學中文.

result.traditional: 因為我想去台灣，所以我想學中文。
result.simplified: 因为我想去台湾，所以我想学中文。
result.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ xiǎng qù Táiwān, suǒyǐ wǒ xiǎng xué Zhōngwén.
result.english: Because I want to go to Taiwan, I want to learn Chinese.

repairs.note: Being tired is the reason, and a reason takes 因為 even when it comes second; 所以 marks a result.
為什麼 asks why; to give the reason, use 因為.
Being tired is a reason not to go: 不想.

items.fallbackRepair: 不 goes before 想, and the reason takes 因為: 我今天不想去學校，因為我很累.

result.traditional: 我今天不想去學校，因為我很累。
result.simplified: 我今天不想去学校，因为我很累。
result.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān bù xiǎng qù xuéxiào, yīnwèi wǒ hěn lèi.
result.english: I don't want to go to school today, because I'm tired.

summary: 因為 brings in the reason, and 所以 brings in the result. The reason usually comes first.
Put 因為 before the reason and 所以 before the result, one in each part.
Don't put 因為 and 所以 together at the start of the sentence.

summary: Put 快, 快要 or 要 before an action to say it is about to happen.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: “在 V” Indicating Ongoing Actions
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what someone is doing right now.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 在 right before an action to say it is happening now. The pattern is Subject + 在 + Verb (Object): 他們在打籃球。
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “在 V” indicates the progressive aspect of an action.

items.question: How do I say “He is playing basketball” — 他是打籃球 or 他在打籃球?
items.answer: 他在打籃球. In this sentence 是 would emphasize a detail; it does not mark the action happening now. Use 在 before the action.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Indicating “from… to…”
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say when a period starts and ends.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 從 before the start and 到 before the end of a period. The range can be hours, days, months, or years: 從四點到五點半.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Indicating “from… to…”, 從……到…… can be used for a temporal duration of time.

summary: Use 從 before the start and 到 before the end of a time range, like 從四點到五點半.

Say the start first, and don't leave out 到.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: First…, then…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Put two actions in order.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 先 before the first action and 再 before the next. If one person does both actions, say the person once: 他先打網球，再游泳.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 先……再…… is a pattern used for sequencing events, much like “First…, then…”. If the subjects are the same, then omit the second one.

items.question: Where does 先 go — before the first action or after it?
items.answer: Before it. 先 + first action, 再 + next action: 我先看書，再做功課.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān kànshū, zài zuò gōngkè.
right.english: I read first, then do homework.

items.question: Is the second marker 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then” in a sequence. 在 is the “at / happening now” word: 我先回家，再去圖書館.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān huí jiā, zài qù túshūguǎn.
right.english: I go home first, then go to the library.

items.question: Where does 再 go when the second person is named?
items.answer: After the second subject: 姐姐先唱，妹妹再唱. Do not put 再 before 妹妹.

right.pinyin: Jiějie xiān chàng, mèimei zài chàng.
right.english: Older sister sings first, then younger sister sings.

summary: Use 先 before the first action and 再 before the next one to say what happens in order.

items.title: Grammar 4–5 · Possibility and comparison

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Vaux 能
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what is possible, allowed, or physically doable.
grammarPages.explanation: 能 has three uses in this lesson: physical ability, permission, and possibility due to outside conditions. 不能 is its negative.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
(1) 能 (physical capability)
(2) 能 (permission)
When indicating permission, 能 could be replaced with 可以. It is commonly used in question forms or negative forms.
(3) 能 (possibility due to objective factors)
能 can indicate possibility due to objective factors which are related to the occurrence of particular events, not inherent in the speakers.

items.question: Where does 能 go — before the subject or before the verb?
items.answer: Before the verb: 他能來嗎？ 能 does not come before the subject.

right.english: Can he come?

items.question: Where does 只 go in 只能?
items.answer: 只 comes before 能: 他只能走. Do not put 只 after the verb.

right.english: He can only walk.

items.question: The picture shows an injured man. Do I say 他能跑 or 他不能跑?
items.answer: Use 不能: 他受傷了，他不能跑. The injury blocks the action.

right.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, tā bù néng pǎo.
right.english: He is injured; he cannot run.

text.traditional: 鳥能飛，人不能飛。
text.simplified: 鸟能飞，人不能飞。
text.pinyin: Niǎo néng fēi, rén bù néng fēi.
text.english: Birds can fly; humans cannot fly.

text.traditional: 他現在只能走，不能跑。
text.simplified: 他现在只能走，不能跑。
text.pinyin: Tā xiànzài zhǐ néng zǒu, bù néng pǎo.
text.english: He can only walk right now; he cannot run.

text.traditional: 我不能喝太多咖啡，因為不能睡覺。
text.simplified: 我不能喝太多咖啡，因为不能睡觉。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù néng hē tài duō kāfēi, yīnwèi bù néng shuìjiào.
text.english: I cannot drink too much coffee, because I won’t be able to sleep.

text.traditional: 現在是上課時間，老師說我們不能看手機。
text.simplified: 现在是上课时间，老师说我们不能看手机。
text.pinyin: Xiànzài shì shàngkè shíjiān, lǎoshī shuō wǒmen bù néng kàn shǒujī.
text.english: It is class time now; the teacher said we cannot look at our phones.

text.traditional: A：在捷運上能吃東西嗎？B：不可以吃東西。
text.simplified: A：在捷运上能吃东西吗？B：不可以吃东西。
text.pinyin: A: Zài jiéyùn shàng néng chī dōngxi ma? B: Bù kěyǐ chī dōngxi.
text.english: A: Can you eat food on the MRT? B: You cannot eat food.

text.traditional: A：我能在這裡用電腦嗎？B：可以，沒問題。
text.simplified: A：我能在这里用电脑吗？B：可以，没问题。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ néng zài zhèlǐ yòng diànnǎo ma? B: Kěyǐ, méi wèntí.
text.english: A: Can I use a computer here? B: Yes, no problem.

text.traditional: 今天我有中文課，不能跟你們去玩。
text.simplified: 今天我有中文课，不能跟你们去玩。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ yǒu Zhōngwén kè, bù néng gēn nǐmen qù wán.
text.english: I have Chinese class today, so I cannot go out with you all.

text.traditional: A：那個地方很遠，我們十點鐘能到嗎？B：沒問題，坐捷運很快。
text.simplified: A：那个地方很远，我们十点钟能到吗？B：没问题，坐捷运很快。
text.pinyin: A: Nàge dìfāng hěn yuǎn, wǒmen shí diǎn zhōng néng dào ma? B: Méi wèntí, zuò jiéyùn hěn kuài.
text.english: A: That place is very far; can we arrive by ten o’clock? B: No problem; taking the MRT is very fast.

text.traditional: A：明天他能來嗎？B：他不能來，因為他女朋友的媽媽要請他吃飯。
text.simplified: A：明天他能来吗？B：他不能来，因为他女朋友的妈妈要请他吃饭。
text.pinyin: A: Míngtiān tā néng lái ma? B: Tā bù néng lái, yīnwèi tā nǚpéngyǒu de māma yào qǐng tā chīfàn.
text.english: A: Can he come tomorrow? B: He cannot come, because his girlfriend’s mother invited him to dinner.

subsections.title: 能 · Physical ability
subsections.explanation: Use 能 or 不能 for what your body is physically able to do.

subsections.title: 能 · Permission
subsections.explanation: For permission, 能 can be replaced with 可以. It is common in questions and negative sentences.

subsections.title: 能 · Outside conditions
subsections.explanation: Use 能 or 不能 when outside events or conditions decide whether something can happen.

practice.title: Answer the following questions. / Complete the following dialogues with 能.

scene.alt: A person holding their throat with a pained expression.

repairs.note: 會 is a skill you learned; he knows how to talk, but his sore throat stops him: 不能.
能 is negated with 不, not 沒: 不能.
要 is about wanting; his throat hurts, so the point is he isn't able: 不能.

items.fallbackRepair: 不 goes right before 能, then the verb: 不能說話.

result.traditional: 他現在不能說話。
result.simplified: 他现在不能说话。
result.pinyin: Tā xiànzài bù néng shuōhuà.
result.english: He can't talk right now.

scene.alt: A man on crutches with one foot in a cast.

repairs.note: 能 is negated with 不, not 沒: 不能.
He knows how to play; the crutches are what stop him, so 不能, not 不會.
Answer with A's verb: A asks 能, so say 不能.

items.fallbackRepair: 不 goes before 能: 不能.

result.traditional: 不能。
result.pinyin: Bù néng.
result.english: No, he can't.

scene.alt: A cup of hot coffee on a saucer with two cookies.

repairs.note: B answers, so the amount goes where A's 多少 was: one cup, as in the picture.
Coffee is counted by the cup: 一杯.

items.fallbackRepair: 只 goes before 能, then the verb and the amount: 只能喝一杯.

result.traditional: 我一天只能喝一杯。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yì tiān zhǐ néng hē yì bēi.
result.english: I can only drink one cup a day.

scene.alt: One woman asks to borrow the car; the owner, holding the keys, raises her palm.

repairs.note: 可以 is negated with 不: 不可以.
不會 is about knowing how to drive; the owner is refusing permission: 不可以.
For permission, 能 and 可以 mean the same: answer with 不可以.

items.fallbackRepair: 不 comes first: 不可以.

result.traditional: 不可以，我今天要用。
result.pinyin: Bù kěyǐ, wǒ jīntiān yào yòng.
result.english: No, you can't. I need it today.

scene.alt: People sitting around a table with laptops in a library.

segments.traditional: 在圖書館裡我們能不能說話？
segments.simplified: 在图书馆里我们能不能说话？

repairs.note: 再 means "then"; people reading right now takes 在 ("in the middle of").
不會 is about not knowing how; the library rule is about being allowed: 不能.

items.fallbackRepair: 不能 answers A; then 在 goes right before the action: 別人在看書.

result.traditional: 不能，別人在看書。
result.simplified: 不能，别人在看书。
result.pinyin: Bù néng, biérén zài kàn shū.
result.english: No, other people are reading.

scene.alt: Above, people at a table with question marks; below, a person asleep on a sofa and another with their head down.

segments.traditional: 為什麼我們不能在樓上跳舞？
segments.simplified: 为什么我们不能在楼上跳舞？

repairs.note: Look at the picture: the sleepers are on the floor below, so 樓下.
再 (zài, "then") only sounds like it; an action going on right now takes 在.

items.fallbackRepair: Where, who, 在, then the action: 樓下有人在睡覺.

result.traditional: 因為樓下有人在睡覺。
result.simplified: 因为楼下有人在睡觉。
result.pinyin: Yīnwèi lóuxià yǒu rén zài shuìjiào.
result.english: Because someone downstairs is sleeping.

alternatives.traditional: 因為有人在樓下睡覺。
alternatives.simplified: 因为有人在楼下睡觉。
alternatives.pinyin: Yīnwèi yǒu rén zài lóuxià shuìjiào.
alternatives.english: Because someone is sleeping downstairs.

scene.alt: A young man at a desk with books and papers; a clock reads 21:00.

segments.traditional: 今天晚上你要不要跟我去百貨公司？
segments.simplified: 今天晚上你要不要跟我去百货公司？

repairs.note: B would be going with A, so 跟你 ("with you"), not 跟我.
能 is negated with 不, not 沒: 不能.

items.fallbackRepair: 不能 comes first, then 跟你, then 去: 不能跟你去.

result.traditional: 我今天有很多功課，不能跟你去。
result.simplified: 我今天有很多功课，不能跟你去。
result.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu hěn duō gōngkè, bù néng gēn nǐ qù.
result.english: I have a lot of homework today, so I can't go with you.

scene.alt: A woman looking worried with an empty coin purse.

segments.traditional: 上課時間快到了，你坐計程車到學校去吧。
segments.simplified: 上课时间快到了，你坐计程车到学校去吧。

repairs.note: 開 is driving it yourself; a passenger 坐 a taxi.
The taxi is what is too expensive: 不能坐計程車.

items.fallbackRepair: 不能 first, then the verb and the taxi: 不能坐計程車.

result.traditional: 太貴了，我的錢不多，不能坐計程車。
result.simplified: 太贵了，我的钱不多，不能坐计程车。
result.pinyin: Tài guì le, wǒ de qián bù duō, bù néng zuò jìchéngchē.
result.english: It's too expensive. I don't have much money, so I can't take a taxi.

scene.alt: Two men near a parcel outside a post office, with a speech bubble showing the 郵 sign.

segments.traditional: 聽說你家附近有郵局，你
segments.simplified: 听说你家附近有邮局，你

segments.traditional: 好，沒問題，我明天幫你寄。
segments.simplified: 好，没问题，我明天帮你寄。

repairs.note: The yes-no form of 能 is 能不能, with 不.
給我寄信 means "mail a letter to me"; B's 幫你寄 shows A wants help: 幫我.

items.fallbackRepair: 能不能 asks the favour, then 幫我: 你能不能幫我寄信？

result.traditional: 聽說你家附近有郵局，你能不能幫我寄信？
result.simplified: 听说你家附近有邮局，你能不能帮我寄信？
result.pinyin: Tīngshuō nǐ jiā fùjìn yǒu yóujú, nǐ néng bu néng bāng wǒ jì xìn?
result.english: I heard there's a post office near your home. Could you mail a letter for me?

summary: 能 has three uses: what your body can do, permission, and what outside conditions allow or block.
For permission, 可以 can replace 能. Permission sentences are common in questions and negatives.
Put 能 or 不能 before the verb, not before the subject.
只 comes before 能: 他只能走.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Implicit Comparison with 比較
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Compare with a known alternative without naming it.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 比較 before a quality when the other side is already known from context. For actions, use 得 to join the action to the quality: 跑得比較快.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 比較 is used to express implicit comparison. If both subjects are known from the context, we can just use the “比較 Vs” pattern.

items.question: Why is 我今天比較是忙 not right?
items.answer: 比較 goes before the quality 忙, and 是 is not needed: 我今天比較忙.

items.question: Can I put 很 and 比較 together?
items.answer: No. Choose one degree word: 今天的天氣比較熱. 很 would say “very hot”, not “hotter than the other day”.

right.english: The weather is warmer today.

items.question: Where does 比較 go when the sentence uses 得?
items.answer: After 跑得: 哥哥跑得比較快. 比較 comes before the quality 快, not before 跑.

right.english: Older brother runs faster.

text.traditional: A：誰比較瘦？B：姊姊比較瘦，妹妹比較胖。
text.simplified: A：谁比较瘦？B：姊姊比较瘦，妹妹比较胖。
text.pinyin: A: Shéi bǐjiào shòu? B: Jiějie bǐjiào shòu, mèimei bǐjiào pàng.
text.english: A: Who is thinner? B: Older sister is thinner; younger sister is heavier.

text.traditional: A：坐飛機比較舒服，還是坐車比較舒服？B：我覺得坐飛機比較舒服。

text.traditional: A：你們兩個人，誰唱歌唱得比較好聽？B：我覺得他唱得比較好聽。
text.simplified: A：你们两个人，谁唱歌唱得比较好听？B：我觉得他唱得比较好听。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen liǎng ge rén, shéi chànggē chàng de bǐjiào hǎotīng? B: Wǒ juéde tā chàng de bǐjiào hǎotīng.

repairs.note: Look at the picture: 國安's room (top) is the bigger one.
A asks which one, so compare with 比較, not 很.
還是 asks "or" in a question; B picks one.

items.fallbackRepair: Whose, 的, then 比較 right before 大: 國安的比較大.

summary: Use 比較 before a quality to mean more, when the other side is already clear from the situation.
With an action, use 得, and put 比較 before the quality, not before the verb: 跑得比較快.
Don't add 是. Don't use 很 and 比較 together: choose one word for how much.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 跟 as a Preposition
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do something with someone, speak to someone, or get something from someone.
grammarPages.explanation: 跟 comes before a person. It can mean “with” (do something together), “to” (speak or ask a person), or “from” (learn or borrow from a person). A helping verb or adverb goes before 跟.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
When 跟 is used as a preposition, it precedes a noun (a person). If a Vaux or an adverb is needed in the sentence, it should precede 跟.
（1） together with
（2） to; with
（3） from

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: In this pattern the subject comes first, then 跟 + the person who joins you: 我跟朋友去醫院。 A different subject can lead, as in 朋友跟我去醫院, but the 跟 phrase still comes before the action.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

right.english: I speak to my friend.

items.question: I speak Chinese to the doctor — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Put 跟 right before the person you speak to: 我跟醫生說中文。 The subject comes first; the 跟 phrase comes before the verb.

right.english: I speak Chinese to the doctor.

summary: 跟 comes before a person. It can mean with, to, or from.
With means doing something together. To means speaking or asking a person. From means learning or getting something from a person.
The 跟 phrase comes before the verb. Words like can, want or always go before 跟.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is a phrase with a modifying clause and a noun. 的 is placed between the clause and the noun. The noun is the main part of this pattern and is placed at the end of it.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Do Something More or Less
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give useful advice with 多 or 少 before an action.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 多 (“more”) or 少 (“less”) directly before an action to give advice.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is used to give some suggestions.

lessonWorld.title: Adjust the advice

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

right.english: Drink more water.

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

right.english: Rest more.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

right.english: You should drink more water.

text.traditional: 你應該多運動，少喝一點兒酒。
text.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō yùndòng, shǎo hē yìdiǎnr jiǔ.

repairs.note: Too thin means eating more, not less: 多吃.
很 goes before a state verb (很瘦); “more” before an action is 多.
太 means “too” (太瘦了); “more” before an action is 多.

items.fallbackRepair: 多 goes before the verb: 多吃一點兒.

segments.traditional: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，應該
segments.simplified: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，应该

repairs.note: Too much coffee means drinking less, not more: 少喝.
To cut down, not stop, use 少: 少喝一點兒.
很 goes before a state verb; “less” before an action is 少.

items.fallbackRepair: 少 goes before the verb: 少喝一點兒.

result.traditional: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，應該少喝一點兒。
result.simplified: 你平常喝太多咖啡了，应该少喝一点儿。
result.pinyin: Nǐ píngcháng hē tài duō kāfēi le, yīnggāi shǎo hē yìdiǎnr.
result.english: You usually drink too much coffee; you should drink a bit less.

repairs.note: 多 goes before an action (a verb), not a thing.
少 goes before an action (a verb), not a thing.

items.fallbackRepair: The exam is coming: study more (多看書) and go online less (少上網).

result.traditional: 快要考試了，你要多看書，少上網。
result.simplified: 快要考试了，你要多看书，少上网。
result.pinyin: Kuài yào kǎoshì le, nǐ yào duō kàn shū, shǎo shàngwǎng.
result.english: The exam is coming; you should read more and go online less.

repairs.note: Being tired all the time calls for more sleep, not less: 多睡覺.
Before a verb, “more” is plain 多: 多睡覺, not 很多睡覺.
太 means “too”; “more” before an action is 多.

items.fallbackRepair: 多 goes before the verb: 多睡覺.

result.traditional: 你應該多睡覺。
result.simplified: 你应该多睡觉。
result.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō shuìjiào.
result.english: You should sleep more.

summary: Put 多 for more or 少 for less directly before an action to give advice, like 多休息.
They go before the action, never after it.
They go with actions, not things. Say 多喝水, not 多水.

items.title: Grammar 4–5 · Future care and if–then plans

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Meaning “Will”
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what you expect will happen.
grammarPages.explanation: 會 before an action can mean “will” — something you expect in the future. A time word makes the future meaning clear.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 會 can be used as a Vaux which means “will”.

lessonWorld.title: Promise the visit
lessonWorld.prompt: The mother promises to buy the socks today.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我今天會去百貨公司幫你買。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我今天会去百货公司帮你买。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān huì qù bǎihuò gōngsī bāng nǐ mǎi.
lessonWorld.english: I will go to the department store and buy them for you today.

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?
items.answer: Before 會. Time first, then 會 + the action: 我明天會來。

right.english: I will come tomorrow.

items.question: Do I add 了 when 會 means something will happen tomorrow?
items.answer: No. 會 already marks the expected future: 我明天會來。 Do not add 了 to the future action.

right.english: I will come tomorrow.

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?
items.answer: 可以 says you are allowed or able. For something you expect to happen, use 會.

right.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn nǐ.
right.english: I will visit you tomorrow.

text.traditional: 老師：你明天要記得帶毛筆來學校。學生：好，我會帶毛筆來。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī: Nǐ míngtiān yào jìde dài máobǐ lái xuéxiào. Xuéshēng: Hǎo, wǒ huì dài máobǐ lái.
text.english: Teacher: Remember to bring your brush to school tomorrow. Student: Okay, I will bring my brush.
text.simplified: 老师：你明天要记得带毛笔来学校。学生：好，我会带毛笔来。

text.traditional: 孩子：媽，妳要幫我買襪子嗎？媽媽：我今天會去百貨公司幫你買。
text.pinyin: Háizi: Mā, nǐ yào bāng wǒ mǎi wàzi ma? Māma: Wǒ jīntiān huì qù bǎihuò gōngsī bāng nǐ mǎi.
text.english: Child: Mom, will you buy socks for me? Mother: I will go to the department store and buy them for you today.
text.simplified: 孩子：妈，你要帮我买袜子吗？妈妈：我今天会去百货公司帮你买。

text.traditional: 宜文：國安生病了，明天會來學校考試嗎？元真：我也不知道。今天下午我們一起去看他吧！
text.pinyin: Yíwén: Guó’ān shēngbìng le, míngtiān huì lái xuéxiào kǎoshì ma? Yuánzhēn: Wǒ yě bù zhīdào. Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒmen yìqǐ qù kàn tā ba!
text.english: Yiwen: Guoan is sick. Will he come to school for the exam tomorrow? Yuanzhen: I do not know either. Let us go visit him this afternoon!

grammarPages.titleEnglish: If…, then…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what should happen if a condition becomes true.
grammarPages.explanation: 要是 or 如果 opens the condition. 就 starts the result. If the subject is the same in both parts, the second subject can be left out.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is used to connect two clauses. The clause with 要是/如果 comes first to put forward an assumption, followed by the other one with 就 to state the result. If the subjects are the same, the second one can be omitted.

grammarPages.pattern: 要是／如果 + Condition， 就 + Result

items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: Where does 了 go in the fever sentence?
items.answer: 了 goes on the condition that has happened: 發燒了. Do not add a second 了 to the result 吃藥.

right.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī yào.
right.english: If you have a fever, take the medicine.

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

right.english: If you have a fever, then rest.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Completed Action with 了
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that an action is completed, with or without a quantity.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 了 after the verb or verb-object to show the action is completed. With a quantity, one 了 reports a finished past action; a second 了 at the end says “so far, and maybe more.”
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
(1) 了 is placed after verb (object) for indicating a completed action.
(2) 了 with Quantified Objects
In this pattern, there is a quantity before the object.
A. Single 了 (with quantified objects)
When using single 了, it indicates the action was completed in the past.
B. Double 了 (with Quantified Objects)
When using double 了, it indicates the action has already been completed so far. It means that the action will probably continue.

items.question: Where does 了 go with a quantity — after the verb or after the object?
items.answer: In this past-action sentence, put 了 after the verb, before the quantity: 我喝了兩杯咖啡. Without 了 before the quantity, the sentence has a different (change-of-state) meaning.

right.pinyin: Wǒ hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi.
right.english: I drank two cups of coffee.

items.question: What does a second 了 add?
items.answer: One 了 reports a finished past action. The final 了 says “so far”: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了 means two cups so far, and more may follow.

right.traditional: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了。
right.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi le.
right.english: I have already drunk two cups of coffee (so far).

items.wrongSimplified: 我已经喝了两杯咖啡了。

items.question: Does 沒 take 了 in a simple past negative?
items.answer: No. 他沒來 means he did not come. 他沒來了 would mean “he is no longer coming”, a different change-of-state meaning.

right.english: He did not come.

summary: Put 了 after the verb to show the action is completed.
With an amount, put 了 right after the verb, before the amount: 我喝了兩杯咖啡. This reports a finished past action.
A second 了 at the end means so far, and more may follow.
Don't add 了 to a simple past negative. 他沒來了 means he is no longer coming.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Tell 沒 and 還沒 Apart
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that a past action did not happen, or has not happened yet.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 沒 before a past action to say it did not happen. Use 還沒 when it has not happened yet but probably will. 了 can mark the question, but not the negative answer.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
(1) with negation marker 沒
A. 沒 is used to negate past actions.
B. 沒（有）can be at the end of the sentence with 了 for questioning.
(2) with negation marker 還沒
It indicates that the action has not happened but it will probably happen.

grammarPages.pattern: 沒 + past action ｜ 還沒 + action not yet done

items.question: For a past action, is it 他昨天不來 or 他昨天沒來?
items.answer: For a simple past action, use 沒: 他昨天沒來. 不 is for present or habitual negation.

right.english: He did not come yesterday.

items.question: What is the difference between 我沒吃 and 我還沒吃?
items.answer: 我沒吃 says I did not eat. 我還沒吃 says I have not eaten yet, and I probably will.

right.english: I have not eaten yet.

items.question: Where does 還沒 go?
items.answer: Before the verb: 我還沒吃. Do not put it after the verb.

right.english: I have not eaten yet.

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 是 + focus + action + 的

patternRows.english: When did they go back to their countries?

items.question: In 是…的, does the sentence end with 了 or 的?
items.answer: Use 的 to close the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天來的. 了 is not the ending here.

right.english: It was yesterday that he came.

items.question: Can I leave out 是 in a negative sentence?
items.answer: No. 是 cannot be left out in a negative sentence: 他不是開車來的.

right.pinyin: Tā bú shì kāichē lái de.
right.english: He did not come by car.

items.question: Where does 的 go?
items.answer: At the end of the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天到的. Do not drop it after the verb.

right.english: It was yesterday that he arrived.

text.traditional: A：他已經到學校了。B：他是幾點到的？A：他是三點三十分到的。
text.simplified: A：他已经到学校了。B：他是几点到的？A：他是三点三十分到的。

text.traditional: A：張先生來了。B：他是開車來的嗎？A：不是，他是走路來的。

text.pinyin: A: Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn hǎo, nǐ shì zài nǎlǐ xué de? B: Wǒ zài Táiwān xué de.
text.english: A: Your Chinese is really good; where did you learn it? B: I learned it in Taiwan.

summary: Use this to stress one detail of something that already happened, such as when, where, who or how.

是 is optional in a positive sentence, but a negative sentence needs it: 他不是開車來的.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Put Steps in Order with 先…等…再…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Arrange a first step, a wait, and the next step.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 先 for the first step, 等 for the condition you wait for, and 再 for the step after it. Without 先, 等…再… still means “wait until…, then…”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
(1) ……，……再…… (not until…)
This pattern indicates the action is not taking place at the moment of speaking. It is not going to take place until a certain time.
(2) 等……，再…… (wait until…)
This pattern expresses that before statement 2 takes place, the subject(s) must wait until statement 1 takes place.
(3) 先……，等……，再…… (first…, wait until…)
先……，等……，再…… is a pattern used for sequencing events.

items.question: Is the “then” word 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then, later” in a sequence. 在 is “at” or “happening now”: 我們晚上再去。

right.english: We will go in the evening.

items.question: What comes first: 等 or the action it waits for?
items.answer: 等 comes before the condition: 等她起床了，你再跟她說. Do not put 再 before 等.

right.traditional: 等她起床了，你再跟她說。
right.pinyin: Děng tā qǐchuáng le, nǐ zài gēn tā shuō.
right.english: Wait until she gets up, then tell her.
right.simplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.wrongSimplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.question: Where does 先 go in 先…等…再…?
items.answer: 先 comes before the first action: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯.
items.wrongTraditional: 你做功課先，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。

right.traditional: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。
right.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā le, zài yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
right.english: Do your homework first, and when Dad is back home, we will have dinner together.
right.simplified: 你先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。

items.wrongSimplified: 你先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。

text.traditional: 這家餐廳今天人太多了，我們以後再來吧。
text.simplified: 这家餐厅今天人太多了，我们以后再来吧。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng jīntiān rén tài duō le, wǒmen yǐhòu zài lái ba.
text.english: This restaurant is too crowded today; let’s come again later.

text.traditional: A：爸爸，這個句子是什麼意思？B：我現在沒空，晚上再告訴你。
text.simplified: A：爸爸，这个句子是什么意思？B：我现在没空，晚上再告诉你。
text.pinyin: A: Bàba, zhège jùzi shì shénme yìsi? B: Wǒ xiànzài méi kòng, wǎnshang zài gàosu nǐ.
text.english: A: Dad, what does this sentence mean? B: I have no time now; I will tell you tonight.

text.traditional: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？B：我今天有一點兒累，我們週末再去吧。
text.simplified: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？B：我今天有一点儿累，我们周末再去吧。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào bu yào gēn wǒ yìqǐ qù dǎqiú? B: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu yìdiǎnr lèi, wǒmen zhōumò zài qù ba.
text.english: A: Do you want to play ball with me? B: I am a little tired today; let’s go this weekend.

text.traditional: 天氣太冷了，等車來了，我們再去外面。
text.simplified: 天气太冷了，等车来了，我们再去外面。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng le, děng chē lái le, wǒmen zài qù wàimiàn.
text.english: It is too cold; wait until the bus comes, then we will go outside.

text.traditional: A：妳決定買這種茶了嗎？B：等我先生也喝了，我們再決定買不買。
text.simplified: A：你决定买这种茶了吗？B：等我先生也喝了，我们再决定买不买。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ juédìng mǎi zhè zhǒng chá le ma? B: Děng wǒ xiānsheng yě hē le, wǒmen zài juédìng mǎi bu mǎi.
text.english: A: Have you decided to buy this kind of tea? B: Wait until my husband has also tried it; then we will decide whether to buy it.

text.traditional: A：這個問題很難，你可以教我嗎？B：我現在要去上課，等下課了再教你，好不好？
text.simplified: A：这个问题很难，你可以教我吗？B：我现在要去上课，等下课了再教你，好不好？
text.pinyin: A: Zhège wèntí hěn nán, nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma? B: Wǒ xiànzài yào qù shàngkè, děng xiàkè le zài jiāo nǐ, hǎo bu hǎo?
text.english: A: This question is hard; can you teach me? B: I am going to class now; I will teach you after class, okay?

text.traditional: A：我們一起去吃飯吧。B：現在去吃飯的人太多了，我想先寫功課，等人少了再去吃。
text.simplified: A：我们一起去吃饭吧。B：现在去吃饭的人太多了，我想先写功课，等人少了再去吃。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù chīfàn ba. B: Xiànzài qù chīfàn de rén tài duō le, wǒ xiǎng xiān xiě gōngkè, děng rén shǎo le zài qù chī.
text.english: A: Let’s eat together. B: Too many people are eating now; I want to do my homework first, then eat when there are fewer people.

text.traditional: A：現在太熱了！B：對啊，我們先去吃冰淇淋，等不熱了，再去海邊玩，好不好？
text.simplified: A：现在太热了！B：对啊，我们先去吃冰淇淋，等不热了，再去海边玩，好不好？
text.pinyin: A: Xiànzài tài rè le! B: Duì a, wǒmen xiān qù chī bīngqílín, děng bú rè le, zài qù hǎibiān wán, hǎo bu hǎo?
text.english: A: It is too hot now! B: Right; let’s eat ice cream first, then go to the beach when it is not hot, okay?

text.traditional: 媽媽：明天妳打算去哪裡？女兒：我要先去朋友家，等百貨公司開了，再去買衣服。
text.simplified: 妈妈：明天你打算去哪里？女儿：我要先去朋友家，等百货公司开了，再去买衣服。
text.pinyin: Māma: Míngtiān nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ? Nǚ’ér: Wǒ yào xiān qù péngyǒu jiā, děng bǎihuò gōngsī kāi le, zài qù mǎi yīfu.

scene.alt: Stacked bowls, an arrow, and hands washing a bowl at a sink.

repairs.note: 在 means “at” or “-ing”; “not until then” is 再: 明天再洗.
先 means “first”; the bowls wait until tomorrow: 明天再洗.
The picture shows the bowls being washed: 洗.

items.fallbackRepair: 再 comes right before the action: 明天再洗.

result.traditional: 碗太多了，我們明天再洗。
result.simplified: 碗太多了，我们明天再洗。
result.pinyin: Wǎn tài duō le, wǒmen míngtiān zài xǐ.

segments.traditional: 百貨公司休息了，我們明天
segments.simplified: 百货公司休息了，我们明天

repairs.note: 在 means “at” or “-ing”; “not until tomorrow” is 再.
先 means “first”; the store is closed today, so the shopping waits until tomorrow: 再.
Tomorrow hasn’t happened yet, so no 了.

items.fallbackRepair: 再 comes right after the time, before the action: 明天再去買東西.

result.traditional: 百貨公司休息了，我們明天再去買東西。
result.simplified: 百货公司休息了，我们明天再去买东西。
result.pinyin: Bǎihuò gōngsī xiūxí le, wǒmen míngtiān zài qù mǎi dōngxi.
result.english: The department store is closed; we’ll go shopping tomorrow instead.

scene.alt: Three panels: a crowded café, a quieter café, and a woman at the CAFE door.

repairs.note: The pictures go from crowded to fewer people: 人少了.
After 等, the change is marked with 了, not 很: 等人少了.

items.fallbackRepair: 等 + the change + 了, then 再 + the action: 等人少了，我再來.

result.traditional: 這家咖啡廳人好多！等人少了，我再來。
result.simplified: 这家咖啡厅人好多！等人少了，我再来。
result.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēitīng rén hǎo duō! Děng rén shǎo le, wǒ zài lái.
result.english: This café is so crowded! I’ll come back when there are fewer people.

scene.alt: Three panels: a woman with a crossed-out food bubble, holding her stomach, and drinking a glass labelled 牛奶.

repairs.note: After a 等 clause, “then” is 再; 在 means “at” or “-ing”.

items.fallbackRepair: 等 + what happens first + 了, then 再 + the action: 等肚子餓了，再喝牛奶.

result.traditional: 她不吃早飯，常常等肚子餓了，再喝牛奶。
result.simplified: 她不吃早饭，常常等肚子饿了，再喝牛奶。
result.pinyin: Tā bù chī zǎofàn, chángcháng děng dùzi è le, zài hē niúnǎi.
result.english: She doesn’t eat breakfast; she often waits until she’s hungry and then drinks milk.

scene.alt: Three panels: a girl eating fruit, a father arriving, and the family eating together.

repairs.note: The child is hungry and not eating yet; 先 says what to do first.
After the 等 clause, “then” is 再; 我們在一起吃飯 would mean we are eating now.
The meal comes after Dad gets home; the first picture shows fruit: 先吃水果.
在 means “at” or “-ing”; here 先 says what to do first and 再 what comes after.

items.fallbackRepair: 先 for the first thing, 再 for what comes after Dad is home: 妳先吃水果…我們再一起吃飯.

result.traditional: 妳先吃水果，等爸爸回家了，我們再一起吃飯。
result.simplified: 你先吃水果，等爸爸回家了，我们再一起吃饭。
result.pinyin: Nǐ xiān chī shuǐguǒ, děng bàba huí jiā le, wǒmen zài yìqǐ chīfàn.
result.english: Eat some fruit first; when Dad gets home, we’ll eat together.

summary: 先 starts the first step, 等 marks what you wait for, and 再 starts the step after.
Without 先, 等…再… still means wait until this happens, then do that.
With a future time word, 再 means the action will happen then, not now: 我們晚上再去.
再 means then or later. Don't write 在 for it.

items.question: Where does 給 go in the book’s pattern?
items.answer: Both 我給她寫信 and 我寫信給她 are correct. The book’s pattern puts 給 before the receiver: 我給她寫信. Do not split it as 我寫信給寫她.

right.english: I write a letter to her.

items.question: Is it 給 or 跟 for “with a friend”?
items.answer: Use 跟 for “with”: 我跟朋友一起去. 給 marks the receiver of an action.

right.english: I go with a friend.

items.question: Where does the receiver go in 哥哥沒給我打電話?
items.answer: After 給: 哥哥沒給我打電話. Do not put the receiver after the verb.

right.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
right.english: My older brother did not call me.

summary: 給 marks the person who receives the action. Put 給 and that person before the verb: 我給她寫信.

To say with someone, use 跟, not 給.

text.traditional: 妳擔心什麼？

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Place 以前 and 以後 on the Timeline
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether something happened before or will happen after a time or activity.
grammarPages.explanation: 以前 means “before” or “in the past”; 以後 means “after” or “in the future.” Use them alone or right after a time or an activity.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
（1） 以前/以後 as simple Time Words
以前 means “previously/formerly”; 以後 means “after wards/in the future”.
（2） 以前/以後 Succeeding Time
a. 以前 means before; 以後 means after.
b. 以前 means ago; 以後 means later, after.
（3） 以前/以後 as Time Words Succeeding Statements
以前 means before; 以後 means after.

items.question: I go home before three. Where does 以前 go?
items.answer: Right after the time: 三點以前. 我以前三點回家 means something else — “I used to go home at three.”

items.question: I want to be a reporter after graduating. Where does 以後 go?
items.answer: Right after the event: 畢業以後. Put it before the event and 以後畢業 means “graduate later.”

items.question: I want to be a reporter someday. Is 半年以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 半年以後 means “six months from now.” For a someday plan, use plain 以後.
