repairs.note: 十分 is a clock minute (十點十分); an amount of time is 十分鐘.
He hasn’t arrived yet, so his arrival is still ahead: 以後.
已經 is for what is done; he hasn’t arrived yet: 十分鐘以後.

items.fallbackRepair: Amount of time first, then 以後: 十分鐘以後.

result.traditional: 我給他打電話了，他說十分鐘以後會到。
result.simplified: 我给他打电话了，他说十分钟以后会到。
result.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā dǎ diànhuà le, tā shuō shí fēnzhōng yǐhòu huì dào.
result.english: I called him; he said he’d be here in ten minutes.

scene.alt: A classroom, an arrow, then two children riding bicycles.

repairs.note: In the first picture class is over and everyone is packing up: 下課.
The arrow goes from class to the bikes, so the ride comes after: 以後.
The first picture is the classroom, not a meal.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以後: 下課以後, not 以後下課.

result.traditional: 下課以後，我們去騎腳踏車。
result.simplified: 下课以后，我们去骑脚踏车。
result.pinyin: Xiàkè yǐhòu, wǒmen qù qí jiǎotàchē.
result.english: After class, we go bike riding.

scene.alt: Hands being washed, an arrow, then a girl eating.

repairs.note: The arrow goes from washing to eating, so washing comes before the meal: 以前.
The second picture shows a meal, not sleep.
The second picture shows a meal, not a class.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以前: 吃飯以前, not 以前吃飯.

result.traditional: 吃飯以前，我都會洗手。
result.simplified: 吃饭以前，我都会洗手。
result.pinyin: Chīfàn yǐqián, wǒ dōu huì xǐ shǒu.
result.english: I always wash my hands before I eat.

scene.alt: A girl brushing her teeth, an arrow, then a girl asleep.

repairs.note: The second picture shows her asleep in bed, not getting up: 睡覺.
The arrow goes from brushing to sleeping, so brushing comes before: 以前.
The second picture shows sleep, not work.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以前: 睡覺以前.

result.traditional: 我睡覺以前要刷牙。
result.simplified: 我睡觉以前要刷牙。
result.pinyin: Wǒ shuìjiào yǐqián yào shuāyá.
result.english: I have to brush my teeth before I go to sleep.

scene.alt: A graduate, an arrow, then a woman doctor.

repairs.note: The arrow goes from graduation to the doctor, so the job comes after: 以後.
The second picture shows a doctor (white coat, stethoscope): 醫生.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以後: 畢業以後想當醫生.

result.traditional: 我畢業以後想當醫生。
result.simplified: 我毕业以后想当医生。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bìyè yǐhòu xiǎng dāng yīshēng.
result.english: After I graduate, I want to be a doctor.

summary: 以前 means before or in the past, and 以後 means after or in the future.
Put them right after a time, a length of time, or an activity, not before it, or the meaning changes.
After a length of time, 以前 means ago and 以後 means later.
For a plan for someday, use plain 以後. 半年以後 means six months from now.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Show an Attitude or Effect with 對
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say who you speak to, what is good or bad for something, and how someone treats another person.
grammarPages.explanation: 對 points toward a person or thing. Use it for the person you speak to, for something that is good or bad for a target, and for how someone treats another person.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
When 對 serves as a preposition, it indicates “to” or “for” and usually precedes a noun.
（1）（speaking） to
（2） for
（3） to; treating（a person）

lessonWorld.title: Point the attitude
lessonWorld.prompt: He treats me well and often helps me.
lessonWorld.traditional: 他對我很好，常常幫我忙。
lessonWorld.simplified: 他对我很好，常常帮我忙。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒ máng.
lessonWorld.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.

items.question: The boss is kind to me. Why does 我 come so early?
items.answer: 對 points at the receiver, so 我 follows it right away: 對我好. English puts “to me” at the end; Chinese does not.

right.english: The boss is kind to me.

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?
items.answer: No — you turned the arrow around. The person right after 對 receives the kindness, so it is 同事對我很好.

right.english: My coworkers are kind to me.

items.question: Phones are bad for my eyes — 對 or 跟 before 眼睛?
items.answer: 對. 對 shows where the effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together with someone.

right.english: Phones are bad for the eyes.

text.traditional: 他常對我說：「我們應該要多運動、多喝水。」
text.pinyin: Tā cháng duì wǒ shuō: “Wǒmen yīnggāi yào duō yùndòng, duō hē shuǐ.”
text.english: He often says to me: “We should exercise more and drink more water.”
text.simplified: 他常对我说：「我们应该要多运动、多喝水。」

text.traditional: 這件事我只對你說，你不要告訴別人。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ zhǐ duì nǐ shuō, nǐ bú yào gàosù biérén.
text.english: I am telling this only to you; do not tell anyone else.
text.simplified: 这件事我只对你说，你不要告诉别人。

text.traditional: 常用手機對眼睛不好。
text.pinyin: Cháng yòng shǒujī duì yǎnjīng bù hǎo.
text.english: Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.
text.simplified: 常用手机对眼睛不好。

text.traditional: 這本書對我不難，我可以學學看。
text.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duì wǒ bù nán, wǒ kěyǐ xuéxue kàn.
text.english: This book is not difficult for me; I can try studying it.
text.simplified: 这本书对我不难，我可以学学看。

text.traditional: 他對我很好，常常幫我忙。
text.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒ máng.
text.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.
text.simplified: 他对我很好，常常帮我忙。

text.traditional: A：老闆對你們怎麼樣？B：他對我們很不錯，常常要我們多注意身體健康。
text.pinyin: A: Lǎobǎn duì nǐmen zěnmeyàng? B: Tā duì wǒmen hěn búcuò, chángcháng yào wǒmen duō zhùyì shēntǐ jiànkāng.
text.english: A: How does the boss treat you? B: He treats us quite well and often tells us to pay more attention to our health.
text.simplified: A：老板对你们怎么样？B：他对我们很不错，常常要我们多注意身体健康。

questions.repairFeedback: Use 對我說.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 對你說.

subsections.title: Speaking to Someone
subsections.explanation: 對 + person before 說 marks the person spoken to.

patternRows.english: He often says to me: “We should exercise more and drink more water.”
I am telling this only to you; do not tell anyone else.

subsections.title: Good or Bad For
subsections.explanation: 對 + person or thing + 好／不好 says who or what is affected.

patternRows.english: Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.
This book is not difficult for me; I can try studying it.

subsections.title: Treating a Person
subsections.explanation: 對 + person + 很好／不錯 describes how someone treats that person.

patternRows.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.

grammarPages.exerciseNote: The book asks you to rearrange four sentences on printed page 281 and prints no answer key; these model answers keep the 對 + person/thing phrase together.

repairs.note: The restaurant is too far, so it is not convenient: 不方便.
給 marks who receives something; “for us” after a judgment is 對我們.

items.fallbackRepair: 對 + the people affected, then 都 and the comment: 對我們都不方便.

result.traditional: 那家餐廳太遠了，對我們都不方便。
result.simplified: 那家餐厅太远了，对我们都不方便。
result.pinyin: Nà jiā cāntīng tài yuǎn le, duì wǒmen dōu bù fāngbiàn.
result.english: That restaurant is too far; it’s inconvenient for all of us.

segments.traditional: 說了很多話，可是有的我不太懂。
segments.simplified: 说了很多话，可是有的我不太懂。

repairs.note: “Say to someone” is 對 + person + 說; 給 goes with 打電話 or 寫信.
在 marks a place; the person spoken to takes 對: 對我說.

items.fallbackRepair: He is the speaker and I’m the one who didn’t understand: 他昨天對我說.

result.traditional: 他昨天對我說了很多話，可是有的我不太懂。
result.simplified: 他昨天对我说了很多话，可是有的我不太懂。
result.pinyin: Tā zuótiān duì wǒ shuō le hěn duō huà, kěshì yǒude wǒ bú tài dǒng.
result.english: Yesterday he said a lot to me, but I didn’t really understand some of it.

alternatives.traditional: 昨天他對我說了很多話，可是有的我不太懂。
alternatives.simplified: 昨天他对我说了很多话，可是有的我不太懂。
alternatives.pinyin: Zuótiān tā duì wǒ shuō le hěn duō huà, kěshì yǒude wǒ bú tài dǒng.
alternatives.english: Yesterday he said a lot to me, but I didn’t really understand some of it.

repairs.note: “Good or bad for” is 對…好: 對身體很好, not 給.

items.fallbackRepair: 對身體 comes before the comment; exercise is good for you, too many sweets are not.

result.traditional: 運動對身體很好，吃太多甜點對身體不好。
result.simplified: 运动对身体很好，吃太多甜点对身体不好。
result.pinyin: Yùndòng duì shēntǐ hěn hǎo, chī tài duō tiándiǎn duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
result.english: Exercise is good for your health; eating too many sweets is bad for your health.

repairs.note: How you treat someone is 對 + person + 很好, not 給.

items.fallbackRepair: 要他 means she tells him to rest, so 李太太 is the one who 對李先生很好; then 下班以後.

result.traditional: 李太太對李先生很好，下班以後常常要他多休息。
result.simplified: 李太太对李先生很好，下班以后常常要他多休息。
result.pinyin: Lǐ tàitai duì Lǐ xiānsheng hěn hǎo, xiàbān yǐhòu chángcháng yào tā duō xiūxi.
result.english: Mrs. Li is very good to Mr. Li; after work she often tells him to rest more.

summary: 對 points to a person or thing: the one spoken to, affected, or treated well or badly.
The person or thing right after 對 receives the speech, effect or kindness: 同事對我很好 means coworkers are kind to me.
Use 對, not 跟, to show where an effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 在學校 · At school

text.traditional: 你昨天怎麼沒來上課？
text.simplified: 你昨天怎么没来上课？
text.pinyin: Nǐ zuótiān zěnme méi lái shàngkè?
text.english: How come you didn’t come to class yesterday?

text.traditional: 我去參加畫畫比賽。你們上課上了什麼？
text.simplified: 我去参加画画比赛。你们上课上了什么？
text.pinyin: Wǒ qù cānjiā huàhuà bǐsài. Nǐmen shàngkè shàng le shénme?
text.english: I participated in a drawing competition. What was the class about?

words.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action

text.traditional: 老師問我們想做什麼工作，大家都說得很高興。
text.simplified: 老师问我们想做什么工作，大家都说得很高兴。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī wèn wǒmen xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò, dàjiā dōu shuō de hěn gāoxìng.
text.english: The teacher asked us what jobs we want to do. Everybody enjoyed talking about it.

words.meaning: links an action to how it went

text.traditional: 我知道友美想當護理師。別的同學呢？
text.simplified: 我知道友美想当护理师。别的同学呢？
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào Yǒuměi xiǎng dāng hùlǐshī. Bié de tóngxué ne?
text.english: I know that Youmei wants to be a nurse. How about the others?

text.traditional: 宜文希望可以用中文和英文工作，所以她以後想當記者，元真想在銀行工作。
text.simplified: 宜文希望可以用中文和英文工作，所以她以后想当记者，元真想在银行工作。
text.pinyin: Yíwén xīwàng kěyǐ yòng Zhōngwén hé Yīngwén gōngzuò, suǒyǐ tā yǐhòu xiǎng dāng jìzhě, Yuánzhēn xiǎng zài yínháng gōngzuò.
text.english: Yiwen wants a job which requires Chinese and English language skills, so she wants to be a reporter in the future. Yuanzhen wants to work for a bank.

text.traditional: 那你畢業以後想做什麼？
text.simplified: 那你毕业以后想做什么？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ bìyè yǐhòu xiǎng zuò shénme?
text.english: What job do you want to do after you graduate from school?

text.traditional: 我以前想當大公司的老闆，可是老闆要做的事情太多，現在覺得當醫生比較好。那你想做什麼？
text.simplified: 我以前想当大公司的老板，可是老板要做的事情太多，现在觉得当医生比较好。那你想做什么？
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián xiǎng dāng dà gōngsī de lǎobǎn, kěshì lǎobǎn yào zuò de shìqing tài duō, xiànzài juéde dāng yīshēng bǐjiào hǎo. Nà nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
text.english: I wanted to be a business owner, but there are so many things to do as a business owner. Now I think being a doctor is better. What do you want to do then?

text.traditional: 當醫生很不錯，但是太忙了，我只想每天可以準時上班、下班。
text.simplified: 当医生很不错，但是太忙了，我只想每天可以准时上班、下班。
text.pinyin: Dāng yīshēng hěn búcuò, dànshì tài máng le, wǒ zhǐ xiǎng měitiān kěyǐ zhǔnshí shàngbān、xiàbān.
text.english: Being a doctor is great, but doctors are too busy. I just want to clock in and clock out on time.

items.title: Grammar 4–5 · Experience and life moments

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Mark a Life Experience with 過
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Talk about experiences you have had, and say you have already done something.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 過 right after a verb for an experience: something you have done before. V過了 relates the finished action closely to now. Use 沒 + verb + 過 for “have not.”
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
（1） 過 indicates completion of an action as an experience.
（2） V過了
It refers to the completion of an action relating more closely to the present moment. It implies that the action has been completed and repetition is unnecessary. It is only used in positive or question forms, not in negative forms.

lessonWorld.title: Add an experience
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker has seen this film.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我看過這部電影。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我看过这部电影。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ kànguo zhè bù diànyǐng.
lessonWorld.english: I have seen this film.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

right.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

right.english: I have worked at a restaurant before.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?
items.answer: 沒. 沒 says the experience never happened. 不 says you refuse or will not do it.

right.english: I have not been to Japan.

text.traditional: 很多台灣人去過日本，因為從台灣到日本不遠。
text.pinyin: Hěnduō Táiwānrén qùguo Rìběn, yīnwèi cóng Táiwān dào Rìběn bù yuǎn.
text.english: Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan, because Japan is not far from Taiwan.
text.simplified: 很多台湾人去过日本，因为从台湾到日本不远。

text.traditional: A：他來過我們家嗎？B：來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bú zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he been to our home? B: Yes; you were not at home then.
text.simplified: A：他来过我们家吗？B：来过，那个时候你不在家。

text.traditional: A：你吃過臭豆腐嗎？B：我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ chīguo chòudòufu ma? B: Wǒ hái méi chīguo, tīngshuō hěn tèbié.
text.english: A: Have you eaten stinky tofu? B: I have not eaten it yet; I hear it is very special.
text.simplified: A：你吃过臭豆腐吗？B：我还没吃过，听说很特别。

text.traditional: A：你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？B：我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I have already eaten; you go eat.
text.simplified: A：你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？B：我吃过了，你们去吃吧！

text.traditional: A：李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？B：她來過了，是早上來的。
text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is coming to our company today. Has she been here? B: She has; she came in the morning.
text.simplified: A：李小姐今天要来我们公司，她来过了吗？B：她来过了，是早上来的。

text.traditional: A：他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？B：我看過了。C：我還沒看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.
text.english: A: He wrote a card for everyone. Have you all seen it? B: I have. C: I have not yet.
text.simplified: A：他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？B：我看过了。C：我还没看。

summary: Put 過 right after a verb to say you have done it before, at any time in life.

V過了 shows the action is already done and does not need repeating. Don't use it in negatives.

items.question: Is 一 required in 看看 / 看一看?
items.answer: No. Both are correct. 一 adds a light “have a look” feel; the repeated verb is the main signal.

items.question: Can I add 了 after a reduplicated verb?

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 就 indicates that something happens earlier or takes place sooner than expected. 就 also indicates that something is easy to be completed or likely to happen.

items.question: Where does 就 go?

A has already arrived (到學校來了), so not 會; 就 marks seven o’clock as early.

items.fallbackRepair: Time first, then 就, then the verb and 了: 七點就到了.

result.traditional: 我七點就到了。
result.simplified: 我七点就到了。

repairs.note: 也 means “also”, but walking forward is the only step; the easy result takes 就.
再 is for a next step you plan; the easy result of 往前走 takes 就.
B is telling A what A will see, so 你.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 goes after the subject and before 可以: 你就可以看到.

result.traditional: 往前走，你就可以看到台北101了。

segments.simplified: 我明天要跟同学介绍我的国家，所以想到图书馆去找书。

repairs.note: 再 is for a next step you plan; the easy result after searching online takes 就.
在 marks an action going on; the easy result after searching online takes 就可以.
想 is what you want; B says it’s easy to find online: 就可以找到了.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 comes first, then 可以: 就可以找到了.

summary: 就 after a time word shows something happens earlier than expected.
就 also introduces an easy result that follows an instruction.
Put 就 after the time word and before the verb: 我六點就起床了.
Without 就, the sentence only reports the time.

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something is about to happen.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 就要 before the event and 了 at the end. A time word usually comes before 就要: 我下個月就要回國了.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This sentence structure indicates the action after 就（要）is going to happen in a very short time. There's usually a time word before this structure. 就（要）means the action is happening soon; 了 is used at the end of the sentence.

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Time + 就要 + Event + 了

patternRows.english: I am going back to my country next month.

items.question: Does 就要…了 need the final 了?
items.answer: The book’s pattern closes with 了: 他明天就要來了. Without 了 the sentence sounds unfinished in this context.

right.pinyin: Tā míngtiān jiù yào lái le.
right.english: He is coming tomorrow.

items.question: Where does 就要 go?
items.answer: Before the event: 圖書館就要關了. A time word goes before 就要.

right.english: The library is about to close.

items.question: Is 快要 also correct?
items.answer: Yes. 快要…了 is another common form. The book uses 就要 in this table; both mean “about to”.

right.pinyin: Tā míngtiān jiù yào lái le.
right.english: He is coming tomorrow.

text.traditional: 他的女朋友明天就要來了，他非常開心。

text.english: His girlfriend is coming tomorrow; he is very happy.

text.traditional: 電影馬上就開始了，他怎麼還沒來？
text.simplified: 电影马上就开始了，他怎么还没来？
text.pinyin: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù kāishǐ le, tā zěnme háiméi lái?

practice.title: Complete the following sentences with 就（要）……了.

repairs.note: 快要 can’t follow a set time like 明天; with a time word use 就要…了.
The exam is tomorrow, still to come, so not 已經; soon after a time word is 就要…了.

items.fallbackRepair: Time word, 就要, the event, 了 at the end: 明天就要考試了.

result.traditional: 明天就要考試了，你不緊張嗎？
result.simplified: 明天就要考试了，你不紧张吗？
result.pinyin: Míngtiān jiù yào kǎoshì le, nǐ bù jǐnzhāng ma?
result.english: The exam is tomorrow. Aren’t you nervous?

repairs.note: 快要 can’t follow a set time like 下星期二; with a time word use 就要…了.
會 doesn’t go with this 了; for something coming up at a set time use 就要…了.

items.fallbackRepair: Subject, time word, 就要, the event, 了: 她下星期二就要回國了.

result.traditional: 她下星期二就要回國了，我想送她一個禮物。
result.simplified: 她下星期二就要回国了，我想送她一个礼物。
result.pinyin: Tā xià xīngqī’èr jiù yào huíguó le, wǒ xiǎng sòng tā yí ge lǐwù.
result.english: She’s going back to her country next Tuesday; I want to give her a present.

repairs.note: 以前 points back in time; “in ten minutes” is 十分鐘以後.
快要 can’t follow a set time like 十分鐘以後; with a time word use 就要…了.

items.fallbackRepair: Time word (十分鐘以後), then 就要, the event 來, and 了.

result.traditional: 火車十分鐘以後就要來了，他們怎麼還沒到？
result.simplified: 火车十分钟以后就要来了，他们怎么还没到？
result.pinyin: Huǒchē shí fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù yào lái le, tāmen zěnme hái méi dào?
result.english: The train is coming in ten minutes. Why aren’t they here yet?

summary: 就要…了 says something is about to happen soon.
Put 就要 before the event and 了 at the end. A time word usually goes before 就要: 我下個月就要回國了.
快要…了 also means about to.

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how long an action lasts.
grammarPages.explanation: Put the duration after the verb. If the verb has an object, repeat the verb before the duration, or use V + duration + 的 + object.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
Time-Duration pattern indicates an action lasts a period of time. In this pattern, the action always precedes Time-Duration.
(1) Main Verbs without Objects
(2) Main Verbs with Objects
A.
B.

lessonWorld.title: Measure the whole journey
lessonWorld.prompt: The group waits ten minutes and visits for three hours.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我們排隊排十分鐘，參觀三個小時。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我们排队排十分钟，参观三个小时。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒmen páiduì pái shí fēnzhōng, cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí.
lessonWorld.english: We wait in line for ten minutes and visit for three hours.

grammarPages.pattern: Action + duration / Verb + object + verb + duration

items.question: Where does the duration go?
items.answer: After the verb: 我每天工作八個小時. Do not put it before the verb.

right.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
right.english: I work eight hours every day.

items.question: What happens when there is an object?
items.answer: Repeat the verb before the duration: 我每天跑步跑三十分鐘.
items.wrongTraditional: 我每天跑步三十分鐘跑。

right.traditional: 我每天跑步跑三十分鐘。
right.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān pǎobù pǎo sānshí fēnzhōng.
right.english: I run thirty minutes every day.
right.simplified: 我每天跑步跑三十分钟。

items.wrongSimplified: 我每天跑步跑三十分钟。

items.question: What does 的 do in 睡七個小時的覺?
items.answer: It joins the duration to the object: seven hours of sleep. Without 的, repeat the verb instead.

right.traditional: 我每天睡七個小時的覺。
right.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuì qī ge xiǎoshí de jiào.
right.english: I sleep seven hours every day.
right.simplified: 我每天睡七个小时的觉。

items.wrongSimplified: 我每天睡七个小时的觉。

text.traditional: 爸爸每天早上運動三十分鐘。
text.simplified: 爸爸每天早上运动三十分钟。
text.pinyin: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang yùndòng sānshí fēnzhōng.
text.english: Dad exercises for thirty minutes every morning.

text.traditional: 我們從學校走十分鐘，就可以到那家銀行了。
text.simplified: 我们从学校走十分钟，就可以到那家银行了。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen cóng xuéxiào zǒu shí fēnzhōng, jiù kěyǐ dào nà jiā yínháng le.
text.english: We walk ten minutes from school and can reach that bank.

text.traditional: 不好意思，請您再等兩分鐘，李先生很快就來了。
text.simplified: 不好意思，请您再等两分钟，李先生很快就来了。
text.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, qǐng nín zài děng liǎng fēnzhōng, Lǐ xiānsheng hěn kuài jiù lái le.
text.english: Sorry, please wait two more minutes; Mr. Li will be here soon.

text.traditional: A：你明天要上課上幾個鐘頭？B：我明天要上課上三個鐘頭。
text.simplified: A：你明天要上课上几个钟头？B：我明天要上课上三个钟头。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ míngtiān yào shàngkè shàng jǐ ge zhōngtóu? B: Wǒ míngtiān yào shàngkè shàng sān ge zhōngtóu.
text.english: A: How many hours of class do you have tomorrow? B: I have three hours of class tomorrow.

text.traditional: A：你每天都運動嗎？B：對，我每天跑步跑三十分鐘。
text.simplified: A：你每天都运动吗？B：对，我每天跑步跑三十分钟。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ měitiān dōu yùndòng ma? B: Duì, wǒ měitiān pǎobù pǎo sānshí fēnzhōng.
text.english: A: Do you exercise every day? B: Yes; I run for thirty minutes every day.

text.traditional: A：你每天做晚飯做兩個小時，不覺得累嗎？B：有時候覺得累，但是我喜歡吃自己做的，所以沒關係。
text.simplified: A：你每天做晚饭做两个小时，不觉得累吗？B：有时候觉得累，但是我喜欢吃自己做的，所以没关系。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ měitiān zuò wǎnfàn zuò liǎng ge xiǎoshí, bù juéde lèi ma? B: Yǒu shíhou juéde lèi, dànshì wǒ xǐhuān chī zìjǐ zuò de, suǒyǐ méi guānxi.
text.english: A: You cook dinner for two hours every day; don’t you feel tired? B: Sometimes I feel tired, but I like eating what I make myself, so it’s okay.

text.traditional: A：我明天要開六個小時的車，我想先去睡覺。B：開六個小時的車一定會很累，你去睡吧。
text.simplified: A：我明天要开六个小时的车，我想先去睡觉。B：开六个小时的车一定会很累，你去睡吧。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ míngtiān yào kāi liù ge xiǎoshí de chē, wǒ xiǎng xiān qù shuìjiào. B: Kāi liù ge xiǎoshí de chē yídìng huì hěn lèi, nǐ qù shuì ba.
text.english: A: I have to drive for six hours tomorrow; I want to sleep first. B: Driving for six hours will surely be tiring; go to sleep.

text.traditional: A：我弟弟很愛玩手機，每天差不多玩五個小時。B：玩五個小時的手機！時間太長了！
text.simplified: A：我弟弟很爱玩手机，每天差不多玩五个小时。B：玩五个小时的手机！时间太长了！
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ dìdi hěn ài wán shǒujī, měitiān chàbuduō wán wǔ ge xiǎoshí. B: Wán wǔ ge xiǎoshí de shǒujī! Shíjiān tài cháng le!
text.english: A: My younger brother loves playing with his phone; he plays about five hours every day. B: Five hours of phone time! That is too long!

words.meaning: links the duration to 手機

text.traditional: A：聽說那個博物館不太遠，只要坐五分鐘的捷運。B：是啊，如果你想走路去也可以，走二十分鐘的路就到了。
text.simplified: A：听说那个博物馆不太远，只要坐五分钟的捷运。B：是啊，如果你想走路去也可以，走二十分钟的路就到了。
text.pinyin: A: Tīngshuō nàge bówùguǎn bú tài yuǎn, zhǐyào zuò wǔ fēnzhōng de jiéyùn. B: Shì a, rúguǒ nǐ xiǎng zǒulù qù yě kěyǐ, zǒu èrshí fēnzhōng de lù jiù dào le.
text.english: A: I heard that museum is not far; it is only a five-minute MRT ride. B: Right; if you want to walk, you can walk there in twenty minutes.

words.meaning: links the duration to 捷運

subsections.title: Verbs without objects
subsections.explanation: Put the duration after the verb.

patternRows.english: I work for eight hours every day.

subsections.title: Verbs with objects: repeat the verb
subsections.explanation: If there is an object, repeat the verb before the duration: 睡覺睡七個小時.

patternRows.english: I sleep for seven hours every day.

subsections.title: Verbs with objects: duration + 的
subsections.explanation: You can also put the duration before 的 and the object: 睡七個小時的覺.

columns.meaning: links the duration to the object

patternRows.english: I sleep for seven hours every day.

practice.title: Rearrange the following sentences. / Rewrite the following sentences with pattern A or B.

repairs.note: 跑 has no object here, so the time comes straight after it: 跑半個小時, no 的.

items.fallbackRepair: Who and when first, then the verb, then how long: 他每天跑半個小時.

result.traditional: 他每天跑半個小時。
result.simplified: 他每天跑半个小时。
result.pinyin: Tā měitiān pǎo bàn ge xiǎoshí.
result.english: He runs for half an hour every day.

alternatives.traditional: 每天他跑半個小時。
alternatives.simplified: 每天他跑半个小时。
alternatives.pinyin: Měitiān tā pǎo bàn ge xiǎoshí.
alternatives.english: Every day he runs for half an hour.

repairs.note: 十分 is a clock time (九點十分); a length of time needs 分鐘: 十分鐘.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb first, then how long: 我需要休息十分鐘.

result.traditional: 我需要休息十分鐘。
result.simplified: 我需要休息十分钟。
result.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào xiūxi shí fēnzhōng.
result.english: I need to rest for ten minutes.

alternatives.traditional: 我需要十分鐘休息。
alternatives.simplified: 我需要十分钟休息。
alternatives.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào shí fēnzhōng xiūxi.
alternatives.english: I need ten minutes to rest.

repairs.note: 睡覺 is verb + object, so the time can’t follow it; use 睡 + 十分鐘.
A yes/no request with 可以 ends with 嗎, not 呢.

items.fallbackRepair: 先 before the verb, the time after it, 嗎 at the end: 可以先睡十分鐘嗎？

result.traditional: 我現在太累了，可以先睡十分鐘嗎？
result.simplified: 我现在太累了，可以先睡十分钟吗？
result.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài tài lèi le, kěyǐ xiān shuì shí fēnzhōng ma?
result.english: I’m too tired right now. Can I sleep for ten minutes first?

segments.traditional: 他每天都走路走半個鐘頭。
segments.simplified: 他每天都走路走半个钟头。

repairs.note: Pattern B splits 走路: 走 + time + 的 + 路.
得 links a verb to a comment; the time joins the object 路 with 的.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern B: verb, time, 的, object: 走半個鐘頭的路.

result.traditional: 他每天都走半個鐘頭的路。
result.simplified: 他每天都走半个钟头的路。
result.pinyin: Tā měitiān dōu zǒu bàn ge zhōngtóu de lù.
result.english: He walks for half an hour every day.

segments.traditional: 我一個星期要上班上五天。
segments.simplified: 我一个星期要上班上五天。

repairs.note: Pattern B splits 上班: 上 + time + 的 + 班.
This is a regular schedule (要, every week), so no 了; join 五天 to 班 with 的.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern B: verb, time, 的, object: 上五天的班.

result.traditional: 我一個星期要上五天的班。
result.simplified: 我一个星期要上五天的班。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yí ge xīngqī yào shàng wǔ tiān de bān.
result.english: I work five days a week.

segments.traditional: 我想上兩個月的華語課。
segments.simplified: 我想上两个月的华语课。

repairs.note: That is the sentence you started with (pattern B); rewrite it with pattern A: repeat the verb, no 的.
A length of months needs 個: 兩個月.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern A: verb + object, the verb again, then the time: 上華語課上兩個月.

result.traditional: 我想上華語課上兩個月。
result.simplified: 我想上华语课上两个月。
result.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shàng Huáyǔ kè shàng liǎng ge yuè.
result.english: I want to take Chinese classes for two months.

segments.traditional: 我明天要坐十六個小時的飛機。
segments.simplified: 我明天要坐十六个小时的飞机。

repairs.note: 開飛機 means flying the plane as the pilot; the sentence is about riding it: 坐.
Pattern A has no 的: verb + object, the verb again, then the time.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern A: verb + object, the verb again, then the time: 坐飛機坐十六個小時.

result.traditional: 我明天要坐飛機坐十六個小時。
result.simplified: 我明天要坐飞机坐十六个小时。
result.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào zuò fēijī zuò shíliù ge xiǎoshí.
result.english: Tomorrow I’ll be on a plane for sixteen hours.

repairs.note: 在 marks an action going on; for how long, repeat the verb: 做功課做兩個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern A: when, verb + object, the verb again, then the time: 每天做功課做兩個小時.

result.traditional: 我每天做功課做兩個小時。
result.simplified: 我每天做功课做两个小时。
result.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zuò gōngkè zuò liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
result.english: I do homework for two hours every day.

repairs.note: 得 links a verb to a comment; the time joins the object 書法課 with 的.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern B: plan, verb, time, 的, object: 打算上一年的書法課.

result.traditional: 他打算上一年的書法課。
result.simplified: 他打算上一年的书法课。
result.pinyin: Tā dǎsuàn shàng yì nián de shūfǎ kè.
result.english: He plans to take calligraphy classes for a year.

repairs.note: 走路 is verb + object, so the time can’t follow it; split it: 走半天的路.

items.fallbackRepair: Pattern B: verb, time, 的, object: 需要走半天的路.

result.traditional: 我明天需要走半天的路。
result.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān xūyào zǒu bàntiān de lù.
result.english: Tomorrow I need to walk for half a day.

repairs.note: 上 goes with a class (上書法課); a language is studied: 學一年的日文.

items.fallbackRepair: Where first, then pattern B: 去日本學一年的日文.

result.traditional: 我決定去日本學一年的日文。
result.simplified: 我决定去日本学一年的日文。
result.pinyin: Wǒ juédìng qù Rìběn xué yì nián de Rìwén.
result.english: I’ve decided to go to Japan and study Japanese for a year.

summary: Put the length of time after the verb, not before it, to say how long an action lasts.
If the verb has an object, repeat the verb before the length of time: 睡覺睡七個小時.
You can also say the verb, the length of time, 的, then the object.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 在博物館門口 · At the museum gate

text.traditional: 博物館五分鐘以後就要開門了，大家都到了吧？
text.simplified: 博物馆五分钟以后就要开门了，大家都到了吧？
text.pinyin: Bówùguǎn wǔ fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù yào kāimén le, dàjiā dōu dào le ba?
text.english: The museum will be open after five minutes. Is everyone here already?

text.traditional: 中明說他快要到了。
text.simplified: 中明说他快要到了。
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng shuō tā kuài yào dào le.
text.english: Zhongming said he’ll be here soon.

text.traditional: 老師，我們要不要先去排隊買票？
text.simplified: 老师，我们要不要先去排队买票？
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒmen yào bu yào xiān qù páiduì mǎi piào?
text.english: Teacher, should we get in line to buy tickets first?

text.traditional: 差不多需要排十分鐘的隊，那好吧，我們先去排隊。
text.simplified: 差不多需要排十分钟的队，那好吧，我们先去排队。
text.pinyin: Chàbuduō xūyào pái shí fēnzhōng de duì, nà hǎo ba, wǒmen xiān qù páiduì.
text.english: It takes about ten minutes to line up. Alright, let’s get in line to buy tickets first.

text.traditional: 今天我們打算參觀三個小時，會有人給我們介紹。進去以後，記得要安靜，不可以說話說得太大聲。
text.simplified: 今天我们打算参观三个小时，会有人给我们介绍。进去以后，记得要安静，不可以说话说得太大声。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen dǎsuàn cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí, huì yǒu rén gěi wǒmen jièshào. Jìnqù yǐhòu, jìde yào ānjìng, bù kěyǐ shuōhuà shuō de tài dàshēng.
text.english: We plan to visit for three hours today. There will be someone introducing the museum for us. After you enter, remember to keep quiet. You can’t speak loudly.

text.traditional: 老師，我剛剛先用手機上網看了很多有趣的圖片，真想馬上就看到博物館裡的東西。
text.simplified: 老师，我刚刚先用手机上网看了很多有趣的图片，真想马上就看到博物馆里的东西。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ gānggāng xiān yòng shǒujī shàngwǎng kàn le hěn duō yǒuqù de túpiàn, zhēn xiǎng mǎshàng jiù kàndào bówùguǎn lǐ de dōngxi.
text.english: Teacher, I just used my cell phone to look for some information on the internet, and I saw many interesting pictures. I want to see what they have in the museum right away.

text.traditional: 我知道你非常喜歡歷史，我想你今天一定會很開心。
text.simplified: 我知道你非常喜欢历史，我想你今天一定会很开心。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nǐ fēicháng xǐhuān lìshǐ, wǒ xiǎng nǐ jīntiān yídìng huì hěn kāixīn.
text.english: I know you like history very much. I think you’ll enjoy it a lot today.

text.traditional: 我也在網路上找了很多文章，那些介紹和故事都非常有趣。
text.simplified: 我也在网路上找了很多文章，那些介绍和故事都非常有趣。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yě zài wǎnglù shang zhǎo le hěn duō wénzhāng, nàxiē jièshào hé gùshi dōu fēicháng yǒuqù.

repairs.note: Before a measure word like 個, the number 2 is 兩: 兩個小時.

scene.alt: A swimmer; two clocks show 6:00 and then 8:00.

repairs.note: The clocks go from 6:00 to 8:00: that is two hours, not eight.
8:00 is when he stopped; after V了 the pattern needs how long: 兩個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: Say the activity, then repeat the verb with 了 and the length: 游泳游了兩個小時.

result.traditional: 他今天早上游泳游了兩個小時。
result.simplified: 他今天早上游泳游了两个小时。

result.english: He swam for two hours this morning.

scene.alt: A girl at a computer; clocks show 7:00 and then 7:30.

repairs.note: 三十分 is a minute on the clock; a length of time is 半個小時.
7:30 is when she stopped; the pattern needs how long: 7:00 to 7:30 is 半個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: Say the activity, then repeat the verb with 了 and the length: 用電腦用了半個小時.

result.traditional: 她昨天晚上用電腦用了半個小時。
result.simplified: 她昨天晚上用电脑用了半个小时。
result.pinyin: Tā zuótiān wǎnshang yòng diànnǎo yòng le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
result.english: She used the computer for half an hour last night.

scene.alt: Four friends singing from song sheets.

repairs.note: Only the verb repeats: 唱歌唱了…, not 唱歌歌了….
上週末 is one weekend, so they sang for hours, not 三年.

items.fallbackRepair: Say the activity, then repeat the verb with 了 and the length: 唱歌唱了三個小時.

result.traditional: 他們上週末唱歌唱了三個小時。

result.pinyin: Tāmen shàng zhōumò chànggē chàng le sān ge xiǎoshí.
result.english: They sang for three hours last weekend.

scene.alt: A girl reading on the floor; 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.

repairs.note: 得 follows a verb to say how it is done; between a length of time and the object, use 的.
From 2:00 to 4:00 is two hours, not four.
4:00 is when she stopped; after V了 the pattern needs how long: 兩個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: V了, then the length, then 的 and the object: 看了兩個小時的書.

result.traditional: 她昨天下午看了兩個小時的書。
result.simplified: 她昨天下午看了两个小时的书。
result.pinyin: Tā zuótiān xiàwǔ kàn le liǎng ge xiǎoshí de shū.
result.english: She read for two hours yesterday afternoon.

scene.alt: A boy studying at a desk; 8:00 PM to 9:30 PM.

repairs.note: 8:00 to 9:30 is an hour and a half: 一個半小時, not just 半個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: V了, then the length, then 的 and the object: 看了一個半小時的書.

result.traditional: 他前天晚上看了一個半小時的書。
result.simplified: 他前天晚上看了一个半小时的书。
result.pinyin: Tā qiántiān wǎnshang kàn le yí ge bàn xiǎoshí de shū.
result.english: He studied for an hour and a half the night before last.

scene.alt: A woman driving; 7:00 AM to 9:10 AM.

repairs.note: 十分 is a minute on the clock; a length of time is 十分鐘.
9:10 is when she stopped; after V了 the pattern needs how long: 7:00 to 9:10.

items.fallbackRepair: Hours before minutes, then 的 and the object: 開了兩個小時十分鐘的車.

result.traditional: 她上週末上午開了兩個小時十分鐘的車。
result.simplified: 她上周末上午开了两个小时十分钟的车。
result.pinyin: Tā shàng zhōumò shàngwǔ kāi le liǎng ge xiǎoshí shí fēnzhōng de chē.
result.english: Last weekend, she drove for two hours and ten minutes in the morning.

summary: Verb + 了 + a length of time says how long a finished action took.
Use only one 了, right after the verb. A 了 at the very end means still going on.
With an object, repeat the verb: 上課上了五個小時. Or put the length of time before the object.
A past time word like 昨天 shows when, but you still need 了 to show it is done.

segments.traditional: 我們等了多久了？小張為什麼還沒來？
segments.simplified: 我们等了多久了？小张为什么还没来？

repairs.note: 多久 asks how long: answer with a length of time, not a clock time like 兩點.
You are still waiting, so use V了 + time + 了; 過 means you did something at some time before.

items.fallbackRepair: 了 after the verb, the length, then 了 again: 等了一個小時了.

result.traditional: 我們等了一個小時了。
result.simplified: 我们等了一个小时了。
result.pinyin: Wǒmen děng le yí ge xiǎoshí le.
result.english: We've been waiting for an hour.

segments.traditional: 你的中文說得真好！你在台灣住了幾年了？
segments.simplified: 你的中文说得真好！你在台湾住了几年了？

repairs.note: 年 takes no measure word: 三年, not 三個年.
三點 is a clock time; 幾年 asks how many years.
幾年 asks how many years, so answer in 年, not 天.

items.fallbackRepair: Number + 年 (no 個), then 了 at the end: 住了三年了.

result.traditional: 我在台灣住了三年了。
result.simplified: 我在台湾住了三年了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ zài Táiwān zhù le sān nián le.
result.english: I've been living in Taiwan for three years.

segments.traditional: 時間還早，你們要回家了嗎？
segments.simplified: 时间还早，你们要回家了吗？

repairs.note: 在 + verb says what is going on right now; to say how long so far, use V了 + time + 了.
過 says you have done something before; to count the time so far, use V了 + time + 了.

items.fallbackRepair: 了 after the verb, the length, then 了 again: 玩了五個小時了.

result.traditional: 我們已經玩了五個小時了，應該回家了。
result.simplified: 我们已经玩了五个小时了，应该回家了。
result.pinyin: Wǒmen yǐjīng wán le wǔ ge xiǎoshí le, yīnggāi huíjiā le.
result.english: We've already been having fun for five hours; we should go home.

scene.alt: A boy at a computer; 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

repairs.note: From 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. is twelve hours, not nine.
點 marks a clock time; a length in hours is 個小時.
He is still at it at 9 p.m., so end with 了: V了 + time + 了.

items.fallbackRepair: Number, 個小時, then 了: 用了十二個小時了.

result.traditional: 他已經用電腦用了十二個小時了。
result.simplified: 他已经用电脑用了十二个小时了。

result.english: He has been on the computer for twelve hours.

scene.alt: Two friends riding bikes; 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM.

repairs.note: Only the verb repeats: 騎腳踏車騎了…, not 騎腳踏車腳踏車….
From 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. is two hours, not nine.

items.fallbackRepair: Repeat the verb with 了, the length, then 了 again: 騎了兩個小時了.

result.traditional: 他們已經騎腳踏車騎了兩個小時了。
result.simplified: 他们已经骑脚踏车骑了两个小时了。
result.pinyin: Tāmen yǐjīng qí jiǎotàchē qí le liǎng ge xiǎoshí le.
result.english: They have been riding their bikes for two hours.

scene.alt: A couple dancing; 8:00 PM to 9:00 PM.

repairs.note: 8:00 is when they started; the pattern needs how long: 8:00 to 9:00 is 一個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: Say the activity, repeat the verb with 了, the length, then 了 again: 跳舞跳了一個小時了.

result.traditional: 他們已經跳舞跳了一個小時了。
result.simplified: 他们已经跳舞跳了一个小时了。
result.pinyin: Tāmen yǐjīng tiàowǔ tiào le yí ge xiǎoshí le.
result.english: They have been dancing for an hour.

scene.alt: Taipei 101 in the rain.

repairs.note: 星期一 is Monday, a day; for how long, say 一個星期 (a week).
得 says how an action is done; between a length of time and 雨, use 的.

items.fallbackRepair: V了, the length, 的 + the object, then 了: 下了一個星期的雨了.

result.traditional: 是啊，已經下了一個星期的雨了。
result.simplified: 是啊，已经下了一个星期的雨了。
result.pinyin: Shì a, yǐjīng xià le yí ge xīngqí de yǔ le.

segments.traditional: 你的中文字寫得真漂亮！

repairs.note: 得 tells how well (寫得真漂亮); for how long, use 了 after the verb and 的 before the object.

items.fallbackRepair: V了, the length, 的 + the object, then 了: 寫了三年的中文字了.

result.traditional: 我已經寫了三年的中文字了。
result.simplified: 我已经写了三年的中文字了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng xiě le sān nián de Zhōngwén zì le.
result.english: I've been writing Chinese characters for three years.

scene.alt: A boy reading at a desk; a woman stands behind him.

segments.traditional: 你先回去吧，我還想在這裡看書。
segments.simplified: 你先回去吧，我还想在这里看书。

repairs.note: 三點 is a clock time; for how long, say 三個小時.

items.fallbackRepair: V了, the length, 的 + the object, then 了: 看了三個小時的書了.

result.traditional: 你已經看了三個小時的書了，不累嗎？
result.simplified: 你已经看了三个小时的书了，不累吗？
result.pinyin: Nǐ yǐjīng kàn le sān ge xiǎoshí de shū le, bú lèi ma?
result.english: You've been reading for three hours already. Aren't you tired?

summary: Use two 了 to say an action began in the past, reaches now, and may continue.
Put the first 了 right after the verb and the second at the very end: 住了半年了.
With an object, repeat the verb before the length of time and keep the final 了.
With only one 了, the action is finished and not still going on.

items.title: Grammar 3 · Compare two sides with 比

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Two Sides with 比
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Compare two people or things and say which has more of a quality.
grammarPages.explanation: Put A before 比 and B after it. Add the adjective or result after 比 + B. 多了／得多 stresses a big difference; 一點兒 means a small difference.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
This sentence structure is used to compare the differences between people, things or matters.
A Vs is needed after 比. The complement can also be an actual quantity and the differences. 得多 and 多了 are used to emphasize that the difference is big; 一點兒 is used to indicate that the difference is not significant.

No 很 after 比 + the other thing; a small difference takes 一點兒 after the adjective.

summary: Use 比 to compare two things: A is the one you describe, and B comes after 比.
Put the describing word at the end, and don't add 很 because 比 already compares.
多了 or 得多 shows a big difference, 一點兒 a small one. The difference can also be an exact amount.
To compare how actions are done, put 得 after the verb: 你來得比我早.

items.title: Grammar 1 · Compare with 跟…(不)一樣

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Things with 跟…(不)一樣
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say two people or things are the same or different.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 跟 between the two things and 一樣 for “the same”. Add 不 before 一樣 for “different”. A describing word can follow 一樣.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
This pattern is used when comparing two or more people, affairs, or things.
A.
B.

grammarPages.pattern: A + 跟 + B + (不)一樣 (+ Describing word)

items.question: Can I compare two things with 一樣 without 跟?
items.answer: No. When you mention the second item, use 跟 before it: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣.
items.wrongTraditional: 越南的生肖中國的不一樣。

right.traditional: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣。
right.pinyin: Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de bù yíyàng.
right.english: Vietnam’s zodiac is not the same as China’s.
right.simplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的不一样。

items.wrongSimplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的不一样。

items.question: What changes 一樣 to 不一樣?
items.answer: Put 不 before 一樣 for “not the same”: 弟弟跟哥哥不一樣聰明. 弟弟跟哥哥一樣不聰明 means both are not smart — a different meaning.
items.wrongTraditional: 弟弟跟哥哥一樣不聰明。

right.traditional: 弟弟跟哥哥不一樣聰明。
right.pinyin: Dìdi gēn gēge bù yíyàng cōngmíng.
right.english: The younger brother is not as smart as the older brother.
right.simplified: 弟弟跟哥哥不一样聪明。

items.wrongSimplified: 弟弟跟哥哥不一样聪明。

items.question: Where does 得 go in the B pattern?
items.answer: Either side can carry 得, but only one: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一樣好 or 他唱歌跟哥哥唱得一樣好. Do not put 得 after both.
items.wrongTraditional: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥唱得一樣好。

right.traditional: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一樣好。
right.pinyin: Tā chànggē chàng de gēn gēge yíyàng hǎo.
right.english: He sings as well as his older brother.
right.simplified: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一样好。

items.wrongSimplified: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一样好。

text.traditional: 這種藥跟那種藥一樣嗎？
text.simplified: 这种药跟那种药一样吗？
text.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào gēn nà zhǒng yào yíyàng ma?
text.english: Is this medicine the same as that medicine?

text.traditional: 這件事情跟那件事情一樣重要。
text.simplified: 这件事情跟那件事情一样重要。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shìqíng gēn nà jiàn shìqíng yíyàng zhòngyào.
text.english: This matter is as important as that matter.

text.traditional: 這棟大樓的電梯跟那棟大樓的（電梯）不一樣大。
text.simplified: 这栋大楼的电梯跟那栋大楼的（电梯）不一样大。
text.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu de diàntī gēn nà dòng dàlóu de (diàntī) bù yíyàng dà.
text.english: The elevator in this building is not the same size as the one in that building.

text.traditional: 他打球，跟哥哥打得一樣好。
text.simplified: 他打球，跟哥哥打得一样好。
text.pinyin: Tā dǎqiú, gēn gēge dǎ de yíyàng hǎo.
text.english: He plays ball as well as his older brother.

text.traditional: 姐姐做飯，做得跟媽媽一樣好吃。
text.simplified: 姐姐做饭，做得跟妈妈一样好吃。
text.pinyin: Jiějie zuòfàn, zuò de gēn māma yíyàng hǎochī.
text.english: Older sister cooks as well as Mom.

text.traditional: 那個美國學生寫字，跟中國人寫得一樣好看。
text.simplified: 那个美国学生写字，跟中国人写得一样好看。

practice.title: Look at the pictures and answer the questions with the pattern “……跟……(不)一樣 (Vs)”.

scene.alt: A younger sister happily drawing beside her younger brother, who looks bored.

segments.traditional: 妹妹的興趣跟弟弟的（興趣）一樣嗎？
segments.simplified: 妹妹的兴趣跟弟弟的（兴趣）一样吗？

repairs.note: Look at the picture: she loves drawing and he is bored, so their interests are not the same: 不一樣.
沒 can’t say “different”: 一樣 is negated with 不, as 不一樣.
比 says one is more than the other; to say same or different, use 跟…(不)一樣.

items.fallbackRepair: 跟 + the second person’s 的, then 不一樣 at the end: 跟弟弟的不一樣.

result.traditional: 妹妹的興趣跟弟弟的不一樣。
result.simplified: 妹妹的兴趣跟弟弟的不一样。
result.pinyin: Mèimei de xìngqù gēn dìdi de bù yíyàng.
result.english: The younger sister’s interests are different from the younger brother’s.

scene.alt: The same girl smiling in two portraits labelled 昨天 and 今天.

repairs.note: She smiles the same yesterday and today, so no 不: 跟昨天一樣好.
一樣 takes the Vs directly, with no 很: 一樣好.

items.fallbackRepair: Compare with 跟 + 昨天, then 一樣 + the Vs: 跟昨天一樣好.

result.traditional: 她今天的心情跟昨天一樣好。
result.simplified: 她今天的心情跟昨天一样好。
result.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de xīnqíng gēn zuótiān yíyàng hǎo.
result.english: She’s in as good a mood today as she was yesterday.

scene.alt: Two sisters running side by side at the same speed.

segments.traditional: 姐姐跑得快，還是妹妹跑得快？
segments.simplified: 姐姐跑得快，还是妹妹跑得快？

repairs.note: 比 picks a winner, but the sisters run side by side at the same speed: 跟妹妹一樣快.
一樣 takes the Vs directly, with no 很: 一樣快.

items.fallbackRepair: After 跑得: 跟 + 妹妹, then 一樣 + 快.

result.traditional: 姐姐跑得跟妹妹一樣快。
result.simplified: 姐姐跑得跟妹妹一样快。
result.pinyin: Jiějie pǎo de gēn mèimei yíyàng kuài.
result.english: The older sister runs as fast as the younger sister.

segments.traditional: 你的美國朋友中文怎麼樣？
segments.simplified: 你的美国朋友中文怎么样？

repairs.note: 得 can’t follow the object 中文; say the verb again: 說中文說得….
比 never goes with 一樣; to say “as well as”, use 跟…一樣好.

items.fallbackRepair: With an object, repeat the verb: 說中文說得跟台灣人一樣好 (or 跟台灣人說得一樣好).

result.traditional: 他說中文說得跟台灣人一樣好。
result.simplified: 他说中文说得跟台湾人一样好。
result.pinyin: Tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de gēn Táiwān rén yíyàng hǎo.
result.english: He speaks Chinese as well as a Taiwanese person does.

alternatives.traditional: 他說中文跟台灣人說得一樣好。
alternatives.simplified: 他说中文跟台湾人说得一样好。
alternatives.pinyin: Tā shuō Zhōngwén gēn Táiwān rén shuō de yíyàng hǎo.
alternatives.english: He speaks Chinese as well as a Taiwanese person does.

summary: Put 跟 between two things, then 一樣 for the same or 不一樣 for different.
You need 跟 before the second thing: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣.
Put 不 before 一樣 to say different. 一樣不聰明 is something else: both are not smart.
With 得, the describing word can follow 一樣. Only one side carries 得.

dialogue.title: 十二生肖 · The Chinese Animal Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 對話一 · Dialogue 1

text.traditional: 我們下個星期要學第十五課，我剛才先看了一點，書上有很多種動物，我覺得很有意思。
text.simplified: 我们下个星期要学第十五课，我刚才先看了一点，书上有很多种动物，我觉得很有意思。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xià ge xīngqí yào xué dì shíwǔ kè, wǒ gāngcái xiān kàn le yìdiǎn, shū shàng yǒu hěn duō zhǒng dòngwù, wǒ juéde hěn yǒuyìsi.
text.english: We are going to study Lesson 15 next week. I just glanced at it earlier. There are many kinds of animals in the book, which I think is very interesting.

text.traditional: 有哪些動物？
text.simplified: 有哪些动物？
text.pinyin: Yǒu nǎxiē dòngwù?
text.english: What animals are there?

text.traditional: 我記得有羊、馬、兔子，最特別的是龍。你看看！
text.simplified: 我记得有羊、马、兔子，最特别的是龙。你看看！
text.pinyin: Wǒ jìdé yǒu yáng, mǎ, tùzi, zuì tèbié de shì lóng. Nǐ kànkan!
text.english: I remember there are goats, horses, rabbits, and the most special one is the dragon. Take a look!

text.traditional: 原來是十二生肖，真的很有意思。
text.simplified: 原来是十二生肖，真的很有意思。
text.pinyin: Yuánlái shì shí'èr shēngxiào, zhēn de hěn yǒuyìsi.
text.english: Oh, so it’s the Chinese zodiac! That’s really fascinating.

text.traditional: 什麼是十二生肖？
text.simplified: 什么是十二生肖？
text.pinyin: Shénme shì shí'èr shēngxiào?
text.english: What is the Chinese zodiac?

text.traditional: 華人用不一樣的動物代表每一年，一共有十二種動物。
text.simplified: 华人用不一样的动物代表每一年，一共有十二种动物。
text.pinyin: Huárén yòng bù yíyàng de dòngwù dàibiǎo měi yì nián, yígòng yǒu shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù.
text.english: Chinese people use different animals to represent each year. There are twelve animals in total.

text.traditional: 越南也有十二生肖，可是我們沒有兔年，有貓年。我是貓年出生的，屬貓。
text.simplified: 越南也有十二生肖，可是我们没有兔年，有猫年。我是猫年出生的，属猫。
text.pinyin: Yuènán yě yǒu shí'èr shēngxiào, kěshì wǒmen méiyǒu tùnián, yǒu māonián. Wǒ shì māonián chūshēng de, shǔ māo.
text.english: Vietnam also has the twelve zodiac animals, but we don't have the Year of the Rabbit; we have the Year of the Cat. I was born in the Year of the Cat, so my zodiac sign is the cat.

text.traditional: 真的？好有趣！原來越南的生肖跟中國的有點不一樣。我好想知道我屬什麼。
text.simplified: 真的？好有趣！原来越南的生肖跟中国的有点不一样。我好想知道我属什么。
text.pinyin: Zhēn de? Hǎo yǒuqù! Yuánlái Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de yǒudiǎn bù yíyàng. Wǒ hǎo xiǎng zhīdào wǒ shǔ shénme.
text.english: Really? How interesting! It turns out Vietnam's zodiac is a bit different from China's. I really want to know what sign I am.

text.traditional: 很簡單，上網一查就知道了。
text.simplified: 很简单，上网一查就知道了。
text.pinyin: Hěn jiǎndān, shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
text.english: It's very simple. Just look it up online and you'll know immediately.

text.traditional: 好，我上網查查看。
text.simplified: 好，我上网查查看。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ shàngwǎng cháchá kàn.
text.english: Okay, I'll search for it online.

comprehension.prompt: 越南的生肖有什麼特別的地方？
comprehension.hint: Listen to Yuanzhen talk about Vietnam's zodiac.

items.title: Grammar 2 · Describe Ongoing States with 著

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe an Ongoing State with 著
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a continuing state or a posture.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 著 directly after a verb to show that the action or state continues: 她看著窗戶外面. The object follows 著.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish:
The particle 著 is placed directly after a verb to indicate the continuation of an action or a state.
(1) “V 著” indicates the continuation of an action.
A.
B. “V 著” indicates a request to maintain a certain action.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

items.question: Where does 著 go?
items.answer: Directly after the verb, before the object: 她看著窗戶外面. Do not put it after the object.

right.english: She is looking outside the window.

items.question: Does 著 mean the action is finished?
items.answer: No. 著 shows a continuing state; 了 shows a completed action. 她看著窗外 is ongoing; 她看了窗外 is completed.

right.english: She is looking outside the window.

items.question: Can an object follow 著?
items.answer: Yes. Put the object after 著: 他拿著燈籠. 著 stays attached to the verb.

right.english: He is holding a lantern.

text.traditional: 他看著窗戶外面，想著他的女朋友。
text.simplified: 他看着窗户外面，想着他的女朋友。
text.pinyin: Tā kàn zhe chuānghu wàimiàn, xiǎng zhe tā de nǚpéngyǒu.
text.english: He is looking outside the window, thinking of his girlfriend.

text.traditional: 他在門口等著你，你快去找他吧。
text.simplified: 他在门口等着你，你快去找他吧。
text.pinyin: Tā zài ménkǒu děng zhe nǐ, nǐ kuài qù zhǎo tā ba.
text.english: He is waiting for you at the door; go find him quickly.

text.traditional: 很多人在那裡唱著歌、跳著舞，大家都很開心。
text.simplified: 很多人在那里唱着歌、跳着舞，大家都很开心。
text.pinyin: Hěn duō rén zài nàlǐ chàng zhe gē, tiào zhe wǔ, dàjiā dōu hěn kāixīn.
text.english: Many people are singing and dancing there; everyone is happy.

text.traditional: 大家聽著，明天一定要準時到。
text.simplified: 大家听着，明天一定要准时到。
text.pinyin: Dàjiā tīng zhe, míngtiān yídìng yào zhǔnshí dào.
text.english: Everyone listen; tomorrow you must arrive on time.

examples.teachingNote: Printed as 1 in part B.

text.traditional: 你看著我，剛才你說的是真的嗎？
text.simplified: 你看着我，刚才你说的是真的吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ kàn zhe wǒ, gāngcái nǐ shuō de shì zhēn de ma?
text.english: Look at me; is what you just said true?

examples.teachingNote: Printed as 2 in part B.

text.traditional: 你在這裡等著，他們馬上就來了。
text.simplified: 你在这里等着，他们马上就来了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèlǐ děng zhe, tāmen mǎshàng jiù lái le.
text.english: Wait here; they are coming right away.

examples.teachingNote: Printed as 3 in part B.

subsections.title: A. A continuing action or state
subsections.explanation: Put 著 after the verb. The object follows 著.

patternRows.english: She is looking at the scenery outside the window.

subsections.title: B. A request to keep an action
subsections.explanation: Use V著 to ask someone to keep doing something: 你們看著我.

patternRows.english: Everyone, look at me; do not read your book.

practice.title: Fill in the blanks using “V 著+O”.

scene.alt: A boy in an armchair watching TV while two people come in through the open door.

repairs.note: He is still watching as we walk in: an action that keeps going takes 著, not 了.
過 says he has done it before; he is watching right now: 看著.
TV is watched, with 看: 看著電視.

items.fallbackRepair: 著 goes right after the verb, before the object: 看著電視.

result.traditional: 中明看著電視，不知道我們已經來了。
result.simplified: 中明看着电视，不知道我们已经来了。
result.pinyin: Zhōngmíng kàn zhe diànshì, bù zhīdào wǒmen yǐjīng lái le.
result.english: Zhongming is watching TV and doesn’t know we’ve already arrived.

scene.alt: A man in a helmet riding a bike fast along a curving road.

repairs.note: He rides off on his bike to go places: the riding keeps going, so 著, not 了.
過 says “has done it before”, which doesn’t fit 常常; here the riding keeps going: 騎著.
開 is for a car; a bike is ridden: 騎腳踏車.

items.fallbackRepair: 著 goes right after the verb, before the object: 騎著腳踏車.

result.traditional: 國安常常騎著腳踏車，到很多地方去玩。
result.simplified: 国安常常骑着脚踏车，到很多地方去玩。
result.pinyin: Guó’ān chángcháng qí zhe jiǎotàchē, dào hěn duō dìfang qù wán.
result.english: Guoan often rides his bike to lots of places to have fun.

scene.alt: A girl with headphones relaxing on a sofa with a mug; books lie nearby.

segments.traditional: 咖啡，覺得很舒服，還不想寫功課。
segments.simplified: 咖啡，觉得很舒服，还不想写功课。

repairs.note: 的 links a describer to a noun; an action that keeps going takes 著 right after the verb.
Coffee is drunk, 喝, and music is listened to, 聽.

items.fallbackRepair: Each verb takes its own 著: 聽著音樂，喝著咖啡.

result.traditional: 宜文聽著音樂，喝著咖啡，覺得很舒服，還不想寫功課。
result.simplified: 宜文听着音乐，喝着咖啡，觉得很舒服，还不想写功课。
result.pinyin: Yíwén tīng zhe yīnyuè, hē zhe kāfēi, juéde hěn shūfu, hái bù xiǎng xiě gōngkè.
result.english: Yiwen is listening to music and drinking coffee; she feels very comfortable and doesn’t want to do her homework yet.

repairs.note: B says 不可以: A must stay, not leave.
To ask someone to keep doing something, use 著: 坐著 means “stay seated”.
過 says “has done it before”; to ask someone to keep doing something, use 著.

items.fallbackRepair: 著 goes right after the verb: 坐著.

result.traditional: 不可以，你坐著，我有事情跟你說。
result.simplified: 不可以，你坐着，我有事情跟你说。
result.pinyin: Bù kěyǐ, nǐ zuò zhe, wǒ yǒu shìqing gēn nǐ shuō.
result.english: No, stay seated. I have something to tell you.

summary: Put 著 right after a verb to show an action or state continues, then put the object after 著.
著 shows a continuing state, while 了 shows a completed action.
V著 can ask someone to keep doing something: 你們看著我.

dialogue.title: 十二生肖 · The Chinese Animal Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 對話二 · Dialogue 2

text.traditional: 中明，你手裡拿著什麼？
text.simplified: 中明，你手里拿着什么？
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng, nǐ shǒulǐ názhe shénme?
text.english: Zhongming, what are you holding in your hand?

text.traditional: 這是燈籠。
text.simplified: 这是灯笼。
text.pinyin: Zhè shì dēnglóng.
text.english: This is a lantern.

text.traditional: 燈籠上的小老虎好可愛。
text.simplified: 灯笼上的小老虎好可爱。
text.pinyin: Dēnglóng shàng de xiǎo lǎohǔ hǎo kě'ài.
text.english: The little tiger on the lantern is so cute.

text.traditional: 這是我朋友做的，因為他屬虎。你知道十二生肖嗎？
text.simplified: 这是我朋友做的，因为他属虎。你知道十二生肖吗？
text.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ péngyǒu zuò de, yīnwèi tā shǔ hǔ. Nǐ zhīdào shí'èr shēngxiào ma?
text.english: A friend of mine made it because he was born in the year of the tiger. Do you know about the twelve zodiac animals?

text.traditional: 知道，友美跟我講過。
text.simplified: 知道，友美跟我讲过。
text.pinyin: Zhīdào, Yǒuměi gēn wǒ jiǎng guò.
text.english: Yes, Youmei mentioned it to me.

text.traditional: 這個星期六是元宵節，你跟友美會去看燈會嗎？
text.simplified: 这个星期六是元宵节，你跟友美会去看灯会吗？
text.pinyin: Zhège xīngqíliù shì Yuánxiāojié, nǐ gēn Yǒuměi huì qù kàn dēnghuì ma?
text.english: This Saturday is the Lantern Festival. Are you and Youmei going to see the lantern show?

text.traditional: 友美說她想去，我還沒決定去不去。燈會好玩嗎？
text.simplified: 友美说她想去，我还没决定去不去。灯会好玩吗？
text.pinyin: Yǒuměi shuō tā xiǎng qù, wǒ hái méi juédìng qù bú qù. Dēnghuì hǎowán ma?
text.english: Youmei said she wants to go, but I haven't decided yet. Is the lantern festival fun?

text.traditional: 我去年去看了，很多大人帶著小孩去看燈會，非常熱鬧。我照了很多相片。
text.simplified: 我去年去看了，很多大人带着小孩去看灯会，非常热闹。我照了很多相片。
text.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián qù kàn le, hěn duō dàrén dàizhe xiǎohái qù kàn dēnghuì, fēicháng rènào. Wǒ zhào le hěn duō xiàngpiàn.
text.english: I went last year. Many adults brought their kids to see the lantern show; it was very lively. I took a lot of pictures.

text.traditional: 那我這個週末一定要去看看。
text.simplified: 那我这个周末一定要去看看。
text.pinyin: Nà wǒ zhège zhōumò yídìng yào qù kànkan.
text.english: Then I must definitely go see it this weekend.

text.traditional: 我週末還要工作，打算一下班就去看燈會。我們可以約友美一起去。
text.simplified: 我周末还要工作，打算一下班就去看灯会。我们可以约友美一起去。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò hái yào gōngzuò, dǎsuàn yí xiàbān jiù qù kàn dēnghuì. Wǒmen kěyǐ yuē Yǒuměi yìqǐ qù.
text.english: I have to work this weekend, but I plan to go see the lantern show right after getting off work. We can invite Youmei to join us.

comprehension.hint: Yiwen asks Zhongming what is in his hand.

items.title: Grammar 3 · Immediate Sequence with 一……就……

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Express Immediate Sequence with 一……就……
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one action happens right after another.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 一 before the first action and 就 before the second: 我一看書，就想睡覺. If the subjects are the same, the second subject is often omitted.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is used to indicate “just as soon as…”. If the subjects of these two clauses are the same, then often one subject is omitted.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Subject 1 + 一 + Action 1，Subject 2 + 就 + Action 2

patternRows.english: Whenever he has a question, he asks the teacher.
As soon as you said it, I understood it.

items.question: Does the pattern need both 一 and 就?
items.answer: For the “as soon as” meaning, use both: 上網一查就知道了. Without 一 the sentence can still be grammatical, but it loses the immediate-sequence meaning.

right.pinyin: Shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
right.english: As soon as you look it up online, you will know.

items.question: Where does 就 go when the second subject is named?
items.answer: After the second subject: 我一說話，他就不高興. Do not put 就 before 他.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yì shuōhuà, tā jiù bù gāoxìng.
right.english: As soon as I speak, he is unhappy.

text.traditional: 我一看書，就想睡覺。
text.simplified: 我一看书，就想睡觉。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yí kànshū, jiù xiǎng shuìjiào.
text.english: As soon as I read, I feel sleepy.

text.traditional: 媽媽一知道我發燒了，就開始擔心。
text.simplified: 妈妈一知道我发烧了，就开始担心。
text.pinyin: Māma yì zhīdào wǒ fāshāo le, jiù kāishǐ dānxīn.
text.english: As soon as Mom knew I had a fever, she began to worry.

text.traditional: 他今天很奇怪，我一說話，他就不高興。
text.simplified: 他今天很奇怪，我一说话，他就不高兴。
text.pinyin: Tā jīntiān hěn qíguài, wǒ yì shuōhuà, tā jiù bù gāoxìng.
text.english: He is strange today; as soon as I speak, he is unhappy.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: As soon as the first action, the second follows.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Rewrite each sentence with 一 before the trigger and 就 before the result.

segments.hint: Use 一 before the first quick action.

questions.correctFeedback: As soon as you search, you know.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 一 before the action.

segments.hint: Use 就 before the immediate next action.

questions.correctFeedback: Going right after work.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 就 before the next action.

segments.hint: As soon as entering the classroom.

segments.traditional: 教室，就看到桌上放著動物。

questions.correctFeedback: Immediately upon entering.
questions.repairFeedback: Pair 一 with the entering verb.

grammarPages.exerciseNote: The book exercise on p.349 gives no answer key; the practice model answers are editorial.

practice.title: Use the pattern “一……，就……” to rewrite the sentences.

segments.traditional: 你到家以後，馬上給我打電話。
segments.simplified: 你到家以后，马上给我打电话。

repairs.note: 給我打電話 means “call me”: 你 gets home and 你 calls, so no 我 here.
一 pairs with 就, not 也: 一…，就….

items.fallbackRepair: Subject first, then 一 + the first action; 就 opens the second part: 你一到家，就….

result.traditional: 你一到家，就給我打電話。
result.simplified: 你一到家，就给我打电话。
result.pinyin: Nǐ yí dào jiā, jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
result.english: Call me as soon as you get home.

segments.traditional: 他說話的時候，大家馬上知道他不是台灣人。
segments.simplified: 他说话的时候，大家马上知道他不是台湾人。

repairs.note: Keep the people of the original: 他 is the one talking and 大家 are the ones who know.
一 pairs with 就, not 也: 一…，就….

items.fallbackRepair: Each person comes first in their part: 他一說話，大家就知道….

result.traditional: 他一說話，大家就知道他不是台灣人。
result.simplified: 他一说话，大家就知道他不是台湾人。
result.pinyin: Tā yì shuōhuà, dàjiā jiù zhīdào tā bú shì Táiwān rén.
result.english: As soon as he speaks, everyone knows he isn’t Taiwanese.

segments.traditional: 這件事我決定了以後，馬上開始做了。
segments.simplified: 这件事我决定了以后，马上开始做了。

repairs.note: 一 + the verb replaces 以後: 一決定 already means “as soon as I decided”.
No 了 in the first part: 一決定; the 了 stays at the end, in 做了.

items.fallbackRepair: 一 goes right before the first verb, and 就 opens the second part: 我一決定，就開始做了.

result.traditional: 這件事我一決定，就開始做了。
result.simplified: 这件事我一决定，就开始做了。
result.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ yì juédìng, jiù kāishǐ zuò le.
result.english: As soon as I decided on this, I started doing it.

summary: Use both 一 and 就 to say that as soon as one thing happens, the next follows.
Put 一 before the first action and 就 before the second: 我一看書，就想睡覺.
If the second action has its own subject, 就 goes after that subject.
If the subjects are the same, the second subject is often left out.

dialogue.title: 有趣的十二生肖 · The Interesting Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 短文 · Reading

text.traditional: 今天一進教室，就看到桌上放著幾隻用紙做的動物，黑板上也有很多張動物的圖片，我覺得很有趣。
text.simplified: 今天一进教室，就看到桌上放着几只用纸做的动物，黑板上也有很多张动物的图片，我觉得很有趣。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān yí jìn jiàoshì, jiù kàndào zhuō shàng fàngzhe jǐ zhī yòng zhǐ zuò de dòngwù, hēibǎn shàng yě yǒu hěn duō zhāng dòngwù de túpiàn, wǒ juéde hěn yǒuqù.
text.english: As soon as I walked into the classroom today, I saw several paper animals placed on the table, and there were also many pictures of animals on the blackboard. I found it very interesting.

text.traditional: 老師告訴我們，很久以前，有十二種動物一起參加了一個過河比賽，看誰游得最快。
text.simplified: 老师告诉我们，很久以前，有十二种动物一起参加了一个过河比赛，看谁游得最快。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī gàosu wǒmen, hěn jiǔ yǐqián, yǒu shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù yìqǐ cānjiā le yí ge guòhé bǐsài, kàn shéi yóu de zuì kuài.
text.english: The teacher told us that a long time ago, twelve animals entered a river-crossing race together to see who could swim the fastest.

text.traditional: 開始比賽以後，每隻動物都游得很快很辛苦。老鼠先過了河，第二個到的是牛，最後到的是豬。老鼠贏了，排第一，其他動物排後面。
text.simplified: 开始比赛以后，每只动物都游得很快很辛苦。老鼠先过了河，第二个到的是牛，最后到的是猪。老鼠赢了，排第一，其他动物排后面。
text.pinyin: Kāishǐ bǐsài yǐhòu, měi zhī dòngwù dōu yóu de hěn kuài hěn xīnkǔ. Lǎoshǔ xiān guò le hé, dì èr ge dào de shì niú, zuìhòu dào de shì zhū. Lǎoshǔ yíng le, pái dì yī, qítā dòngwù pái hòumiàn.
text.english: After the race began, each animal swam hard and fast. The rat crossed the river first, the ox arrived second, and the pig arrived last. The rat won, ranking first, and the other animals lined up behind.

text.traditional: 這次比賽以後，華人就用鼠、牛、虎、兔、龍、蛇、馬、羊、猴、雞、狗和豬代表每一年，而且叫這十二種動物「十二生肖」。
text.simplified: 这次比赛以后，华人就用鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗和猪代表每一年，而且叫这十二种动物「十二生肖」。
text.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài yǐhòu, Huárén jiù yòng shǔ, niú, hǔ, tù, lóng, shé, mǎ, yáng, hóu, jī, gǒu hé zhū dàibiǎo měi yì nián, érqiě jiào zhè shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù "shí'èr shēngxiào".
text.english: After this race, Chinese people used the rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog, and pig to represent each year, calling these twelve animals the "Twelve Zodiac Animals".

text.traditional: 華人聊天的時候，會問別人「你屬什麼？」。每年到了元宵節，代表那年的動物燈籠，也會最受歡迎。
text.simplified: 华人聊天的时候，会问别人「你属什么？」。每年到了元宵节，代表那年的动物灯笼，也会最受欢迎。
text.pinyin: Huárén liáotiān de shíhòu, huì wèn biérén "nǐ shǔ shénme?". Měi nián dào le Yuánxiāojié, dàibiǎo nà nián de dòngwù dēnglóng, yě huì zuì shòu huānyíng.

items.title: Grammar 1 · Distances with 離

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say How Close or Far Two Places Are with 離
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how far one place is from another.
grammarPages.explanation: 離 means “from” in a distance phrase. Put the first place before 離, the second place after it, then an adverb and 遠 (far) or 近 (close).

teachingGlossary.pinyin: zuò sān ge xiǎoshí de fēijī

grammarPages.pattern: Place A + 離 + Place B + Adverb + 遠／近

patternRows.english: My home is very far from the company.
Japan is really close to Taiwan.
The bank is not too far from here.

items.question: Can I say how far two places are without 離?
items.answer: No. 離 is the word that names the distance. Without it, the sentence does not compare two places.

right.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
right.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
right.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

items.question: What is the difference between 離 and 從?
items.answer: 離 tells a distance between two places. 從 tells where a trip starts. Use 離 for distance.

right.english: The school is far from the hospital.

items.question: Where does 很近 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the second place. The pattern is Place A 離 Place B 很近.
items.wrongTraditional: 離火車站百貨公司很近。
items.wrongSimplified: 离火车站百货公司很近。

right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

text.traditional: A：我們下個月去日本玩，好不好？ B：好啊，日本離臺灣真的很近，坐三個小時的飛機就到了。
text.simplified: A：我们下个月去日本玩，好不好？ B：好啊，日本离台湾真的很近，坐三个小时的飞机就到了。

text.english: A: Let us go to Japan next month, okay? B: Sure, Japan is really close to Taiwan; a three-hour flight and you are there.

summary: 離 means from. It tells how far or close two places are.
Say the first place, 離, the second place, then a word like 很 and 遠 or 近.
You can't leave 離 out, because it is the word that names the distance.
Don't use 從 for distance. 從 tells where a trip starts.

dialogue.title: 在台灣旅行 · Traveling in Taiwan
dialogue.setting: 對話一 · Dialogue 1

text.traditional: 國安，這次學校放假，你有什麼計畫？
text.simplified: 国安，这次学校放假，你有什么计划？
text.pinyin: Guó'ān, zhè cì xuéxiào fàngjià, nǐ yǒu shénme jìhuà?
text.english: Guo'an, school is going on vacation this time. Do you have any plans?

text.traditional: 我還沒打算要做什麼。這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪裡比較好。
text.simplified: 我还没打算要做什么。这次放假，没有上次放得那么久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪里比较好。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi dǎsuàn yào zuò shénme. Zhè cì fàngjià, méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ, zhǐ fàng sān tiān jià, wǒ bù zhīdào qù nǎlǐ bǐjiào hǎo.
text.english: I haven't decided what to do yet. This break is not as long as the last one—only three days—so I don't know where it's best to go.

text.traditional: 我覺得太魯閣不錯，有山又有河。
text.simplified: 我觉得太鲁阁不错，有山又有河。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde Tàilǔgé búcuò, yǒu shān yòu yǒu hé.
text.english: I think Taroko Gorge is great; it has both mountains and rivers.

text.traditional: 在哪裡？離台北遠不遠？
text.simplified: 在哪里？离台北远不远？
text.pinyin: Zài nǎlǐ? Lí Táiběi yuǎn bù yuǎn?
text.english: Where is it? Is it far from Taipei?

text.traditional: 在花蓮。花蓮在台灣東部，離台北有點遠，你可以坐火車去，也可以開車去，差不多四個小時。
text.simplified: 在花莲。花莲在台湾东部，离台北有点远，你可以坐火车去，也可以开车去，差不多四个小时。
text.pinyin: Zài Huālián. Huālián zài Táiwān dōngbù, lí Táiběi yǒudiǎn yuǎn, nǐ kěyǐ zuò huǒchē qù, yě kěyǐ kāichē qù, chàbùduō sì ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: It's in Hualien. Hualien is in eastern Taiwan, somewhat far from Taipei. You can take a train or drive there; it takes about four hours.

text.traditional: 你去過嗎？
text.simplified: 你去过吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ qù guò ma?
text.english: Have you been there?

text.traditional: 我小學六年級的時候去過，我很喜歡那裡。
text.simplified: 我小学六年级的时候去过，我很喜欢那里。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoxué liù niánjí de shíhòu qù guò, wǒ hěn xǐhuān nàlǐ.
text.english: I went when I was in sixth grade of elementary school. I liked it very much.

text.traditional: 那你打算去哪裡玩？
text.simplified: 那你打算去哪里玩？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ wán?
text.english: Where do you plan to go for fun?

text.traditional: 我想去合歡山。報紙上寫，這幾天可能會下雪。
text.simplified: 我想去合欢山。报纸上写，这几天可能会下雪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Héhuān Shān. Bàozhǐ shàng xiě, zhè jǐ tiān kěnéng huì xiàxuě.
text.english: I want to go to Hehuanshan. The newspaper says it might snow these few days.

text.traditional: 下雪？我還沒看過雪，合歡山在哪裡？
text.simplified: 下雪？我还没看过雪，合欢山在哪里？
text.pinyin: Xiàxuě? Wǒ hái méi kàn guò xuě, Héhuān Shān zài nǎlǐ?
text.english: Snow? I haven't seen snow before. Where is Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 在台灣的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.simplified: 在台湾的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān de zhōngbù, Rìyuè Tán yě zài fùjìn.
text.english: In central Taiwan. Sun Moon Lake is also nearby.

text.traditional: 日月潭很有名，我在書上看過，離合歡山近嗎？
text.simplified: 日月潭很有名，我在书上看过，离合欢山近吗？
text.pinyin: Rìyuè Tán hěn yǒumíng, wǒ zài shū shàng kàn guò, lí Héhuān Shān jìn ma?
text.english: Sun Moon Lake is very famous. I read about it in a book. Is it close to Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 不遠，我想去玩三天兩夜，先去日月潭，再去合歡山。
text.simplified: 不远，我想去玩三天两夜，先去日月潭，再去合欢山。
text.pinyin: Bù yuǎn, wǒ xiǎng qù wán sān tiān liǎng yè, xiān qù Rìyuè Tán, zài qù Héhuān Shān.
text.english: Not far. I want to go for three days and two nights: go to Sun Moon Lake first, and then to Hehuanshan.

text.traditional: 你記得多照一些相片給我看！
text.simplified: 你记得多照一些相片给我看！
text.pinyin: Nǐ jìdé duō zhào yìxiē xiàngpiàn gěi wǒ kàn!
text.english: Remember to take more pictures for me to see!

items.question: Do I keep 來 or 了 at the very end?
items.answer: The changed part ends with 了. 後來 sits before the changed part, not at the end.

items.question: Can I use only 後來 to show a change?
items.answer: A change story reads better with both parts. 本來 (or 原來) starts it, and 後來 gives the change.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。

repairs.note: On its own, 以後 means “in the future”; this already happened, so use 本來 for the plan and 後來 for what changed.
然後 just lists the next step; this sentence needs 本來 for the plan and 後來 for the change.

items.fallbackRepair: 本來 tells the first plan, 後來 what happened later: 本來想去…，可是後來下雨了.

result.traditional: 我們本來想去日月潭，可是後來下雨了，就沒去。
result.simplified: 我们本来想去日月潭，可是后来下雨了，就没去。
result.pinyin: Wǒmen běnlái xiǎng qù Rìyuètán, kěshì hòulái xià yǔ le, jiù méi qù.
result.english: We had planned to go to Sun Moon Lake, but then it rained, so we didn’t go.

repairs.note: 然後 just lists the next step; this sentence needs 本來 for how it was and 後來 for the change.
會 is negated with 不, not 沒: 不會.
On its own, 以後 means “in the future”; this already happened, so use 本來 for how it was and 後來 for the change.

items.fallbackRepair: 本來 + 不會 tells how it was at first, then 後來 + the change: 他本來不會，後來學會了.

result.traditional: 會。他本來不會，後來學會了。
result.simplified: 会。他本来不会，后来学会了。
result.pinyin: Huì. Tā běnlái bú huì, hòulái xuéhuì le.
result.english: Yes. He couldn’t at first, but later he learned.

summary: 本來 or 原來 says how things were at first, and 後來 says what changed or really happened.
Use both parts in a change story. 本來 and 原來 mean the same here.
Put 後來 before the changed part, not at the end: 後來買車了.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Two Things as Even More with 更
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one thing has even more of a quality than another.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 更 before the adjective to raise the degree: A 比 B 更 + adjective.
grammarPages.pattern: A + 比 + B + 更 + Adjective

patternRows.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.
My older brother’s grades are even better than mine.
Kaohsiung’s weather is even warmer than Taipei’s.

items.question: Can I compare with only 更?
items.answer: For a two-thing comparison you also need 比. The shape is thing 比 thing 更 + describing word.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Where does 更 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word. It is not after the second thing.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Does 更 mean the most?
items.answer: No. 更 means even more between two things. Say 最 for the most among a group.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

text.traditional: A：你的成績比你弟弟好嗎？ B：對，可是我哥哥的成績比我更好。
text.simplified: A：你的成绩比你弟弟好吗？ B：对，可是我哥哥的成绩比我更好。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ de chéngjī bǐ nǐ dìdi hǎo ma? B: Duì, kěshì wǒ gēge de chéngjī bǐ wǒ gèng hǎo.
text.english: A: Are your grades better than your younger brother’s? B: Yes, but my older brother’s grades are even better than mine.

text.traditional: 今年的表演比去年的更有意思，我覺得你應該來看。
text.simplified: 今年的表演比去年的更有意思，我觉得你应该来看。
text.pinyin: Jīnnián de biǎoyǎn bǐ qùnián de gèng yǒu yìsi, wǒ juéde nǐ yīnggāi lái kàn.
text.english: This year’s performance is even more interesting than last year’s; I think you should come see it.

text.traditional: 我覺得家人和朋友都很重要，但家人比朋友更重要。
text.simplified: 我觉得家人和朋友都很重要，但家人比朋友更重要。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde jiārén hé péngyǒu dōu hěn zhòngyào, dàn jiārén bǐ péngyǒu gèng zhòngyào.
text.english: I think family and friends are both important, but family is even more important than friends.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Choose 比 and 更 to make the comparison.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Finish each comparison.

segments.hint: Put 比 between the two things.

questions.correctFeedback: Use 比 to show the two things.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 比 between the two things.

segments.hint: Use 更 before the describing word.

questions.correctFeedback: The describing word needs 更.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 更 before the describing word.

segments.hint: Use 比 between the two things.

questions.correctFeedback: Start the comparison with the two things.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 比 between the two things.

grammarPages.exerciseNote: The book writes three sentences with S1 比 S2 更 Vs on printed page 385; these model answers follow the printed prompts.

repairs.note: A 比 sentence never takes 很; for “even more”, use 更.
離 is for distance; to compare two places, use 比.
Taipei is already cold and the mountain gets snow, so it is even colder: 冷, not 熱.

items.fallbackRepair: 比 + the other place, then 更 + the state verb: 合歡山比台北更冷.

result.traditional: 對，可是合歡山比台北更冷，還會下雪。
result.simplified: 对，可是合欢山比台北更冷，还会下雪。
result.pinyin: Duì, kěshì Héhuānshān bǐ Táiběi gèng lěng, hái huì xià xuě.
result.english: Yes, but Hehuan Mountain is even colder than Taipei; it even snows there.

repairs.note: 最 means “the most” and never goes in a 比 sentence; for “even more”, use 更.
A 比 sentence never takes 很; for “even more”, use 更.
更 means “even more”: 哥哥 is already tall, so 爸爸 is even taller: 高, not 矮.

items.fallbackRepair: 比 + the person, then 更 + the state verb: 爸爸比哥哥更高.

result.traditional: 哥哥高，可是爸爸比哥哥更高。
result.pinyin: Gēge gāo, kěshì bàba bǐ gēge gèng gāo.
result.english: My older brother is taller, but Dad is even taller than him.

summary: 更 means even more when you compare two things.
Use 比 too, and put 更 right before the describing word: 今天比昨天更冷.
更 doesn't mean the most. Use 最 for the most in a group.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Link Two Finished Actions with 就
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one finished action is followed immediately by another.
grammarPages.explanation: Finish the first action with 了, then use 就 before the next action. The second action follows right away.

teachingGlossary.pinyin: zuótiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
teachingGlossary.meaning: last night I took a shower

teachingGlossary.pinyin: měitiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
teachingGlossary.meaning: every night I take a shower
ending word: something is done or has changed

grammarPages.pattern: First action + 了 + 就 + Next action

subject.pinyin: zuótiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
subject.meaning: last night I took a shower

columns.pinyin: zuótiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
columns.meaning: last night I took a shower

patternRows.english: Last night after taking a shower, I went right to sleep.

subject.pinyin: měitiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
subject.meaning: every night I take a shower

columns.pinyin: měitiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
columns.meaning: every night I take a shower

patternRows.english: Every night after taking a shower, I go right to sleep.
When we got to the mountain, we saw snow everywhere.

items.question: Where does the first 了 go?
items.answer: Right after the first action. 就 comes before the next action.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I need 就 between the two actions?
items.answer: Yes. 就 is the word that links the finished action to what happened right after.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do both actions need 了?
items.answer: The first action takes 了 to show it is finished. The next action may also end with 了.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

text.traditional: 昨天晚上我洗了澡，就睡覺了。
text.simplified: 昨天晚上我洗了澡，就睡觉了。
text.pinyin: Zuótiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo, jiù shuìjiào le.
text.english: Last night after taking a shower, I went right to sleep.

text.traditional: 我每天到了教室，就開始準備上課。
text.simplified: 我每天到了教室，就开始准备上课。
text.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dào le jiàoshì, jiù kāishǐ zhǔnbèi shàngkè.
text.english: Every day as soon as I arrive in the classroom, I begin preparing for class.

text.traditional: 他明年畢了業，就要去參觀朋友的工廠。
text.simplified: 他明年毕了业，就要去参观朋友的工厂。
text.pinyin: Tā míngnián bì le yè, jiù yào qù cānguān péngyǒu de gōngchǎng.
text.english: Next year after graduating, he is going to visit his friend’s factory.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Put 了 after the first action and 就 before the next.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Finish each two-action sentence.

segments.hint: Use 就 before the next action.

questions.correctFeedback: The next action comes right after.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 就 before the next action.

segments.hint: Use 就 to link the two actions.

questions.correctFeedback: The next thing happened right away.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 就 to link the two actions.
